You can find the new reports in the Reports section of Procountor’s main menu. The number of reports you see depends on your Procountor access rights. (You can check the required access rights in our user manual.)

 

Old Graphical Reports Will Be Removed in October – No Further Updates Will Be Made

The old graphical reports will be phased out on October 31st as they become unnecessary. 

Here is a list of the reports that will be removed (and for which updated versions will be released):

  • Sales Reporting
  • Purchase Reporting
  • Travel and Expense Reporting
  • Salaries Reporting
  • Cash Flow Report
  • Management Reporting
  • Management Reporting by Dimension
  • Register-dimension reporting

No further updates or changes will be made to these outdated reports. This allows us to focus our resources on developing and releasing the new replacement reports as quickly as possible.

We apologize for any update issues or downtime with your old graphical reports. The new reports are designed to avoid any similar performance issues.


Report Development Continues – and We Want to Hear Your Opinion!

We will continue to improve the reports even after their release. We are eager to hear your thoughts and experiences with the new reports – please feel free to contact us! You can provide feedback directly from the report view in Procountor or by using this feedback form.

Kind regards,
Procountor Team

articles.name: Purchase reporting
articles.title: Purchase reporting
articles.body:
You can access the Purchases report in Reporting > Purchase reporting.

The reporting system retrieves the information in real time from Procountor's database. 

Purchases reports help you monitor purchases according to products and suppliers.

Please notice! If the user has Dimension-specific limitation in use, the purchases report is not available.

 

User rights

In order for the user to view the purchase report, they must have at least the following user rights:

  • Rights for purchase invoices: Viewing rights or All rights
  • Search purchase invoices: Viewing rights or All rights
  • No limitation in use: Access only purchase invoices created by user
  • No limitation in use: Access only invoices user can approve or verify
  • No additional feature in use: Dimension-specific limitation

 

Search criteria

  1. First, define the search criteria for the report.
  2. Click Apply.
  3. The program generates purchases reports in line with the search criteria.

The report can be filtered with the following criteria:

 

Time period

  • Current period
  • Last 6 months
  • Last 12 months
  • Current year
  • Custom period
    • Start and End: Free date definition either by filling values in the fields or by using the calendar icon. 
    • The data of the report is retrieved from purchase invoices by default by invoice date.

 

Products

The Product button opens the product selection. You can search for products, product groups and invoice products.

  • Products: The section displays all the products entered into the product register, regardless of whether they have been used in invoices.
  • Product groups: The section displays the purchase product groups used to search for products in said product group.
  • Invoice products: The section only displays the products used in invoices. The product does not have to be set up in the product register.

Search field: You can filter the list by entering any part of the name of products, product groups and invoice products.

 

Suppliers

The Suppliers button opens the supplier selection. You can search for suppliers, supplier groups and invoice suppliers.

  • Suppliers: The section displays all the suppliers who have been entered in the suppliers register.
  • Supplier groups: The section displays the supplier groups used to search for purchases in said supplier group.
  • Invoice suppliers: The section displays only the suppliers with a registered invoice. The supplier does not have to be set up in the supplier register.

Search field: You can filter the list by entering the name or the first few characters of the suppliers, supplier groups and invoice suppliers.

 

Figures

  • EUR: purchases in EUR excluding value added tax (the name of the button is according to the currency of the country of the Procountor's environment).
  • EUR + VAT: purchases in EUR including value added tax (the name of the button is according to the currency of the country of the Procountor's environment).
  • Quantity: number of products in purchase invoices.

 

Invoice dates or receipt dates

  • You can choose whether to search for purchases invoices according to invoice date or receipt date.

 

Transactions

  • All transactions: searches for both business transactions and other transactions.
  • Business transactions: searches for business transactions, in other words receipts with the status approved, payment queued, payment sent to bank, partly paid, paid, marked paid.
  • Others transactions: searches for other than business transactions. 

 

Create report

Apply makes the program search for information in line with the search criteria.

Reset to default clears your selections and resets the default search criteria.

View details allows you to browse the content of the graphs at row level.  The Export to excel –button on the opening  Purchases invoice rows –view exports the report data to an Excel file.

 

Purchases overview

The topmost graph presents the general purchases development in line with the search criteria. 

You can track the development of purchases per year, month or day, for example. In the drop-down menu of the Show button, select one of the following:

  • Yearly
  • monthly
  • daily
  • weekly
  • half-year
  • Quarter

You can select various graph types. In the Graph type drop-down menu, select one of the following:

  • Periodic 
  • Cumulative purchases
  • Purchases compared to previous year 
  • Cumulative purchases compared to previous year 
  • Purchases difference % to previous year

The graph can be saved as a PNG-format image file by clicking on the Export to PNG button. 

 

Purchases by product, product group and invoice product

The middle graph in the view examines the purchases at the product level.

 

Filtering the information

  • On the header row of the graph, you can select whether to browse the graph per product, product group or invoice product. 
    • On the Products -tab, purchases are displayed listed according to the products in the product register.
    • On the Invoice products -tab, purchases are displayed according to the products entered on the invoices. The tab shows the products that have not been added to the product register or the product name differs from the product name in the register.
  • In the table, you can choose to view a product, a product group or an invoice product by clicking on the product's name, for example. Reselect the same row to reset the filters.

Buttons

  • The Export to excel –button exports the table data to an Excel file.
  • The Table can be expanded or minimized with the  icon. 
  • From the  button, you can drill down from product table to invoices, so that you can see which invoices are related to chosen product.
    • From the Invoices’ view, it is possible to drill down to the individual invoice by clicking the invoice number. 

 

Purchases by Supplier, Supplier groups and Invoice suppliers

The bottom graph in the view examines purchases at supplier level. 

 

Filtering the information

  • On the header row of the graph, you can select whether to browse the graph per supplier, supplier group or invoice suppliers.
    • On the Suppliers - tab, purchases are displayed listed according to the suppliers in the Procountor's  suppliers register.
    • On the Invoice suppliers -tab, purchases are displayed according to the suppliers appearing on the invoices. The tab shows the purchase invoices of suppliers who have not been added to the suppliers register or whose name differs from the name in the register.
  • In the table, you can choose to view a supplier, a supplier group or an invoice suppliers by clicking on the supplier's name, for example. Reselect the same row to reset the filters.

Buttons

  • The Export to excel –button exports the table data to an Excel file.
  • The Table can be expanded or minimized with the  icon. 
  • From the  button, you can drill down from suppliers  table to invoices, so that you can see which invoices are related to chosen supplier.
    • From the Invoices’ view, it is possible to drill down to the individual invoice by clicking the invoice number. 

 

Note on the visibility of comparative data in the report

The figures for the comparison period (e.g. the previous year) to not always match the actual figures for the period. 

  • If the search criteria include Products: All and / or Suppliers: All, the Purchases by Product and Purchases by Supplier tables will only show those products / suppliers that have purchases in the current period.
  • If you want to include products / suppliers that do not have purchases in the current period but have purchases in the comparison period, you need to select the products / suppliers separately through the Products and Suppliers search criteria.

articles.name: Procountor internal Information channel
articles.title: Procountor internal Information channel
articles.body:
Procountor has adopted a new information channel that provides information on new program features, product updates and other important matters related to the use of the program.

You can also read Procountor's support articles via the new Help center at the bottom of the left menu. 

The information channel is available on Procountor from the version update of February 17, 2024, onwards, and it will be implemented in stages: we will start by publishing a part of our bulletins on the channel and extend its use for other communication later.

 

Targeted and timely information

Via the information channel, we can offer you and other Procountor users targeted and useful information. The information channel enables us to limit the visibility of the information to the user groups who need it. For example, if we are renewing the preparation of sales invoices, we can share the information about the changes only with the users who create sales invoices. Similarly, users who are not affected by the change will not have to read information that is irrelevant to them.

 

Instructions are conveniently available directly in the program

The Help center contains instruction manuals relating to the use of Procountor. It can be found at the bottom of the left menu.  You can read the instructions easily without leaving Procountor. Use the Search function to search for instructions. 

 

Manage the visibility of information in the communication settings

Our information channel enables us to share only useful information with you, such as presentations of new functions and information on changes to services and disruptions. The aim of our communication is to make using the program as smooth as possible and present functions an services that can make your work more efficient.

You can change the In-App communications settings in Procountor under Personal information and settings whenever you wish. We do not recommend disabling the Procountor service disruptions so as to ensure that you receive information about incidents as soon as possible. 

Sharing targeted bulletins requires that we use data that we have collected about you and your use of Procountor, such as cookies. However, you may prevent the use of the data in Procountor under Personal information and settings by disabling the collection of data. After this, you will not see targeted bulletins in Procountor. The Help center of the menu is not hidden even if the settings are changed. 

More information on the communication settings is available here.

articles.name: Notes for the turn of the year 2025-2026
articles.title: Notes for the turn of the year 2025-2026
articles.body:
You can create salary lists in 2025 for the year 2026. Calculating salaries for 2026 requires that the salary base of each employee is updated.

Salary bases can be updated from December 4, 2025 onwards and the instructions for this update can be found in this article. The employer contribution percentages for 2026 are available starting on December 4, 2025.

Available in Procountor on December 4, 2025:

  • Social insurance contributions
  • Accommodation benefit values
  • Updated values for salary types

Car benefit values and the car benefit calculator will be updated on December 13, 2025.

Available in Procountor on January 1, 2026:
Travel and expense product register, e.g., daily allowances for foreign travel. Travel invoices for next year can be created starting January 1, 2026.

 

Last banking day of the year

  • Salaries paid as SEPA salaries with a payment date of December 31, 2025, must be sent to the bank for processing no later than 30.12. Your own bank can give you more information on bank-specific cut-off times and payment deadlines.
  • We recommend making any payments for the year 2025 well before the cut-off times.

 

Changes to fringe benefits

  • In car benefit calculation, the previous monthly deduction of €85 for plug-in hybrid cars (CO₂ emissions 1–100 g/km) will be removed starting January 1, 2026.

 

Changes to salary types

  • No changes to salary types.

 

Changes to income types

  • There are no changes to income types.

 

Retrieving Tax Cards

The retrieval of payroll tax cards is done through the Withholding percentage request view (Payroll > Withholding percentage request). Tax cards must still be retrieved manually in Procountor. The Finnish Tax Administration has already released automatic retrieval, and this feature will also be updated in Procountor in early 2026.

 

When will the 2026 tax card be available for fetching?

Tax cards will be available in the Tax Administration's MyTax service by 6.12 at the latest, and after that, tax cards for 2026 can be fetched through Procountor's Withholding percentage request view. The 2026 tax card will take effect on 1.1.2025.

The Tax Administration's service states:

Your tax card for 2026 will be sent to MyTax between 22 November and 6 December 2025. If you still receive paper mail, the tax card will be delivered to you by post by the end of December.

The tax card will be valid as of 1 January 2026. As soon as your tax card is shown in MyTax, you can make changes to it or request a revised tax card.

Activate Suomi.fi Messages to receive a notification when the tax card arrives in MyTax.

 

Revised tax cards

The employee can make changes to the tax card or order a new tax card as soon as the employee has received the 2026 tax card in MyTax.

We recommend informing employees by when the revised tax card should be requested so that tax cards are included when you retrieve tax card information for 2026 through Procountor's Withholding percentage request view.

 

Are tax cards retrieved automatically?

The Finnish Tax Administration has already released automatic retrieval, and this feature will also be updated in Procountor in early 2026. Currently, tax cards must be retrieved manually through Procountor's Withholding percentage request view.

 

Employee pension contribution and upper age limit for insurance

The employee pension contribution will be standardized, and in 2026 it will be the same for all employees aged 17–69: 7.3% regardless of age.

Additionally, starting in 2026, the upper age limit for TyEL insurance will depend on the employee’s year of birth:

Employees born in 1958–1961 must be insured until age 69.

Employees born in 1962 or later must be insured until age 70.

Please check the employee’s year of birth and ensure TyEL insurance continues to the correct age limit, even when the employee turns 68.

 

Paying salaries at the end of the year

Changes to salary percentages

 

Updating salary bases and employer contribution percentages

To calculate salaries for 2026 the employees’ salary bases must be updated. Before updating the salary bases it is recommended that all salaries for the year 2025 are paid to avoid having to change, for example, the travel expense salary type values for 2025.

 

Calculating salaries for 2026 can be done as follows:

Please note that when creating payroll calculations for 2026, the employee must have a new 2026 tax card retrieved before generating the payroll list. Otherwise, tax will automatically be withheld at 60%.

1. The update can be done by creating a new salary list (Payroll > New salary list) with a payday in 2026. When the payday is set to 2026, Procountor requests to update the salary bases.

2. Click the Update salary bases -button.

3. Procountor will copy Working hour reduction settings and / or equalization table values to the next year if they don’t exist yet.  Copying will be done automatically when creating a new salary list for new year. We will make copying only for active settings which are assigned to employees.

The following have been now updated:

  • Travel expense 
  • Accident insurance percentages
  • Working hour reduction settings 
  • Equalization tables under working hour reduction settings 

  • Travel expense salary type values have been updated to the new 2026 values.
  • The travel expense products in the payroll type register for 2026 will be updated to reflect the 2026 values.

4. If you have employees that are using custom values for their accident insurance percentage or the car and accommodation benefit, Procountor provides a list of these employees.

  • It is possible to update employee's custom accident insurance percentages directly to a row. New percentages will be updated to the employees' information.
    • If an employee no longer needs a custom accident insurance percentage, you can update the percentage to be the same as in the company settings. After that the employee doesn't show up on this list anymore for having a custom percentage
  • If you have employees with Car or Accommodation benefit, make sure to update their values to the salary base manually.

5. Press Continue -button.

The lists of employees that might require actions are not available after continuing. Export the lists if you wish to access them later.

6. Check the employer payment percentages.

  • Make sure that the Salaries basic info view (in Management > Salary info > Salaries basic info) has the correct percentages for employer’s payment for 2026. To see the percentages for 2026, select the year from the drop-down menu.
  • By default, the employer’s payment percentages are updated to the default percentages.
  • When creating a salary list with the payday in the year 2026, Procountor will use the employer’s payment percentages selected in the Salaries basic info.

6. After the salary bases have been updated, you may continue working on the salary lists and salary slips.

 

What withholding tax percentage should be used on January’s salaries?

  • The 2026 tax cards will enter into effect on 1 January 2026.
  • The income ceiling stated on the tax card is calculated for the full year.
  • The employee can make changes to the tax card or order a new tax card as soon as the 2026 tax card is in MyTax. From 6.12.2025 onwards, everyone can make changes or order a new tax card for 2026.
  • Read more in the Tax administartion's page.

 

I updated the salary bases but need to calculate salaries for 2025. What should I do?

  • Salary slips can still be created for the year 2025.
  • When the payday of the salary list is in 2025, Procountor automatically used the employer contribution percentages of 2025.
  • When creating a salary slip, make sure the employee accident insurance contribution percentage matches the percentage of 2025.
  • Make sure that the travel expense salary type values match the 2025 travel expense salary type values.
  • Make sure that the car and accommodation benefit values match the 2025 values of these benefits.

 

Holiday pay reservation

  • To check the holiday pay reservation for December, the Holiday reports (Reports > Salary reports > Holiday reports) must be run before calculating salaries for January, since the dates for the report cannot be selected.
  • If salaries have already been calculated for January, they will be shown on the report.

 

Start of the year version update January 1, 2026

  • Version update for the end of 2025 / beginning of 2026 will update the new 2026 travel invoice and expense claim product prices.
  • The values for travel expense salary types selected from the salary type register for salary slips will be updated to the 2026 values.

 

Travel invoices

  • Kilometer allowance and per diem values will change at the beginning of 2026.
  • Products with the product code “v2025” should be used on invoices dated to the year 2025 and products with the code “v2026” on invoices dated to 2026. The new products will be released at the start of the year.
  • 2025 products will be available in the product register for January and February 2026.
  • Travel invoice payment date must be in 2025 to include these travel invoices on the 2025 earnings payment report.

 

The general VAT change in Procountor 

The VAT rate is decreasing from 14% to 13.5% on January 1, 2026.

A separate instruction page has been created on this topic, where we have compiled key points about the VAT change from the Procountor user’s perspective. Click here to access the guide.

 

Updates to the EU VAT percentages in 2026

  • The VAT percentages of different EU countries will be updated to Procountor, after the European commission has confirmed the changes to these percentages. These foreign VAT percentages for different EU countries are available to users who have specifically requested the free special right Foreign VAT for their Procountor environment.
  • If you need additional VAT percentages sooner, please contact our customer service, and we will attempt to update these percentages sooner.
  • The foreign VAT special right enables the handling of sales and purchase invoices of a VAT liable company in another EU country. The VAT percentage of this particular country is selected on the invoice and the VAT is reported to the local tax authority.

articles.name: Holiday setting change in the middle of holiday credit year
articles.title: Holiday setting change in the middle of holiday credit year
articles.body:
It is possible to have more than one holiday earning rule within one holiday credit year (HCY) in Procountor. There might be a need for this e.g. in following cases:

  • Employee’s duties change impacting contract and thus possibly also the holiday earning rules. Example:  1.4. – 30.6. holiday earning rule 14d and percentage calculation method and 1.7. onwards 35h rule and average hourly calculation method. Two earning rules within same holiday credit year.
  • Employee’s contract has ended, but he comes back to a new employment, with same or different holiday earning rules. Example: 1.6. -31.8. earning rule 35h and average hourly calculation method. Employment ended and holidays are paid off. Employee comes back to a new employment 1.12.-31.12. with same holiday earning rules, but the holiday earning start day changes -> new holiday earning rule. From this employment the holidays are not paid off as his contract is changed to permanent employment from 1.1. onwards but with different holiday earning rules: 14d and average hourly calculation method. Then there are three holiday earning rules during holiday credit year.

Note: If holiday earning rules change during holiday credit year, the salary payment periods need to match with holiday setting periods. Example: Monthly payment periods, but holiday settings change 14.5. thus old setting period is 1.4.-14.5. and new setting period is 15.5. - 31.3. Salary list periods for the employee in May need to be as follows: 1st salary list 1.-14.5. and 2nd salary list 15.5.-31.5. This way the holiday day and earnings can be directed to the correct holiday setting. Procountor will notify and guide while creating salary lists if these cases exist.

 

When should you have a new setting?

There are a few conditions to create a new setting:

  • If there are no salary slips for the current holiday setting, there is no need to create a new setting (prevented). You can modify the existing setting.
  • If there are unfinished salary slips, a new setting cannot be created.
  • There can be no salary slips within the period where the new setting is created for. There should be no manually edited earned holiday days either in the Edit monthly figures for that period.

Which changes require a new setting creation?

  • Holiday/holiday bonus earning start date change (e.g. new employment)
  • Holiday earning rule change 14d/35h/right for time off
  • Collective agreement change (if the change is within the collective agreement, no new setting is required, then you can Recalculate the year)
  • Calculation base change, with few exceptions:
    • You can still change monthly calculation basis into percentage without creating a new setting. Note, that if the holiday earning rule change at the same time e.g. 14d to 35h, then you need to create a new setting. You can edit the first setting (just not change the 14d rule) and create a new setting with 35h and percentage calculation basis.
    • Monthly calculation basis into another monthly basis (standard and workday divider)

 

How to create a new setting

Setting is created in the Payroll > Employee register > Holidays tab.

There is a drop-down menu next to Edit holiday earning rules. It contains the existing editing of holiday earning rules and Create a new setting.

Select Create a new setting and enter the first day when this new setting is valid from. This will automatically set the previous day as the end date for the previous setting. Give the new holiday earning rules and save.

New field appears next to the holiday credit year, that shows the holiday setting periods. As a default the latest setting is visible when entering the Holidays tab. From the drop-down menu you can check/edit the old setting.

The top of the Holidays tab shows all the holiday credit year data including all the holiday setting periods within them. The cumulative holiday days, holiday bonus days and holiday pay/holiday bonus pay etc.

Note that if the holiday credit year contains multiple setting periods, they might contain 0,5 earned days, which are rounded up as per setting. But the top rounds per holiday credit year. Investigation is still ongoing on the correct handling process.

 

The impact of multiple holiday setting periods on other Employee register Holidays functionalities:

Edit setting period figures (previously Edit yearly figures) works now on setting period level, so that e.g. the extra holidays (not earned via salary slips) can be calculated with correct holiday calculation basis.

  • Edit monthly figures shows the whole holiday credit year, even if they comprise from different holiday settings. Fields change based on the settings. You can edit earned days for any holiday setting even via the latest setting. The change will take place in the correct setting.
  • If by the end of holiday credit year the employee earns additional holiday days, add them to the last holiday setting period.
  • Recalculation-button works on holiday setting period level. Ie if you have modified multiple collective agreement settings, you need to recalculate all of the setting periods individually.
  • Set-up holiday data > Select file doesn’t support different holiday setting periods for one employee.

If an employee doesn’t have multiple holiday settings during holiday credit year, then the views and functions remain mainly the same (few titles/button names have changed).

 

Earning holiday days and holiday bonus days

Earning of holiday days and bonus days are according to the setting. If employee has multiple settings in a holiday credit year, earned holiday days and bonus days are collected per setting period, but can been seen via any setting (via monthly view).

Manual editing of holiday and holiday bonus days can be done via any setting. Editing of additional leave days should be done via the last holiday setting period.

If setting has been changed in the middle of the month, please note that the earning according to 14 days rule or 35 hours rule (depending on the selected setting) can be met in only one setting period, the old or in the new one and if none of them meets the rule, user might need to adjust the earned holiday days and bonus days manually.

 

Earning cumulative earnings which affect holiday pay

Salary slip can be created with only one holiday pay setting and the cumulative earnings are belonging to the setting within that salary period.

Manual editing of cumulative earnings can be only done via the specific holiday setting period.

 

Paying holidays in salary slip – New Holiday pay pop up

We have created a new Holiday pay pop up, which will replace the existing holiday pay pop up.

In the new Holiday pay pop up first user needs to select the right event type: Holiday pay, Holiday bonus or Additional leave days. After selecting the wanted event type user is able to see available amount of holiday/bonus/additional leave days per holiday credit year and also employee’s holiday pay settings.

After the wanted row has been selected the wanted amount of holiday/bonus/additional leave days can be set to the selected row in the Holiday days to be paid column. Add to slip will close the Holiday pay pop up and insert the right salary type with inserted number of days to the salary slip.

Holiday compensation for Right for time off can be found behind Holiday pay event type.

Please note that also holiday days and holiday bonus days which are earned from the current slip are displayed in the Available amount column in Holiday pay pop up.

When the calculation basis is Monthly with standard divider, you need to enter the holiday days to be paid and the quantity of the workdays. The calendar and calculation logic have been removed.

 

Paying holidays in salary slip – Multiple holiday pay settings

If employee has multiple holiday pay settings in a holiday credit year, all of them are displayed below according to setting period and the available amount of holiday/bonus/additional leave days are shown in the rows.

It’s possible to select multiple holiday days from different rows if the holiday pay setting is the same. Holiday days from different holiday credit years/holiday periods will be displayed in their own salary rows in the salary slip.

Salary type is provided automatically according to the holiday pay setting.

It is not possible to pay more holiday/bonus/additional leave days than the employee has earned.

 

Correcting paid holidays in salary slip -multiple holiday pay settings

Correcting paid holiday days/bonus days for employees with multiple holiday pay settings is done the same way as for employees with only one holiday pay setting. With multiple holiday pay settings paid holiday/bonus days are displayed below according to setting period and the Available amount to correct holiday/bonus/ days are shown in the rows. It’s possible to correct multiple holiday days from different rows if the holiday pay setting is the same.

 

Holiday accrual report

Holiday accrual report has been modified to take into account also multiple setting periods. Report is showing only the current holiday pay setting.

 

One year holiday earning rule check

The most automated update still takes place in Management > Salary info > Holiday credit years > Review one year earning rule.

View shows the employee on several rows, if the employee has more than one holiday setting period during  holiday credit year. When you select one row, then other rows for the employee are automatically selected.

View shows what changes take place within the holiday setting periods. And if you decide to update the previously earned holiday days/holiday bonus days, then all holiday setting periods are updated.

In case the holiday bonus earning start date is later than the holiday earning start date, it will show up separately on the Review one year earning rule -view.

You can do more controlled change via the Employee register > Holidays, in case collective agreements have differing rules from the Annual Holidays Act. Note, here the change impacts only one holiday setting period at a time.

 

Handling of unsupported holiday earning settings

The earlier changes made in holiday settings in the middle of holiday credit year and the impacted earned holiday days still need to be paid outside holiday pay functionality with manual salary types.

 

Deleting a holiday setting

Deleting a holiday setting is possible with certain criteria, when:

  • no slips are created (if any are created, they need to be invalidated).
  • no manual or imported adjustments to values (days or earnings).

The first setting of the holiday credit year cannot be deleted as each holiday credit year needs to have at least one setting.

To delete a setting, first select the setting to delete from the Setting period -drop down menu. In this example a setting has been created for period 1.7.2024 - 31.3.2025.

Click the arrow icon next to the Edit holiday earning rules, choose Delete the current setting. Confirm deletion.

 

The holiday credit year now has the original setting for 1.4. - 31.3., and a new setting can be created for the employee.

articles.name: Procountor Junior Dimensioning
articles.title: Procountor Junior Dimensioning
articles.body:
What is Procountor Junior Dimensioning?

  • Junior Dimensioning is an artificial intelligence assistant that predicts dimensions and dimension item to on purchase invoices' Verification view.
  • As Junior Dimensioning makes these dimension suggestions, the user’s responsibility is to check and verify their correctness.
  • Junior Dimensioning can be enabled on all purchase invoices or only on certain invoices.
  • Junior Dimensioning must be enabled by the customer – it will not be automatically enabled.
  • Junior Dimensioning is separate from Posting predictions Junior. They can, however, be used at the same time. They both have different usage settings.
    • Junior Dimensioning does not make changes to postings, VAT statuses and VAT deduction right percentages.

Procountor Junior Dimensioning is available with a monthly fee. Read more about the pricing here.

 

How to enable Junior Dimensioning?

What is required to enable Junior Dimensioning?

To make it possible to enable Junior Dimensioning, the following conditions must be met:

  • There must be within 50 purchase invoices within 12 months that are considered business transactions.
    • This means that the invoices must be either Approved, Payment denied, Payment queued, Payment sent to bank, Partly paid, Marked paid, or Paid.
  • Purchase invoices must be posted by row.
    • This can be checked on the Usage settings view (Management > Company info > Usage settings).
  • The environment must be a Finnish Procountor environment.
  • The environment must be in production. Environments in trial usage do not support Junior Dimensioning.
  • Junior can only be enabled in Procountor Financials environments (not Alku or Light version).

 

Where and how can Junior Dimensioning be enabled?

If the above-mentioned conditions are met, Junior Dimensioning can be enabled either on the Verification view of a purchase invoice with the guided setup or alternatively on the Usage settings view.

Enabling Junior Dimensioning on the purchase invoice Verification view:

  • If the above-mentioned conditions are met, Procountor Dimensioning will suggest enabling Junior when the user opens the purchase invoice Verification view.
  • A pop-up window explaining the basics of Junior Dimensioning and how effectively Junior Dimensioning would work in that particular Procountor environment.
    • Two options are displayed: I would like to try Junior Dimensioning and Continue without Junior Dimensioning.
    • To enable Junior, select I would like to try Junior Dimensioning. This enables Junior Dimensioning for all the suppliers and all purchase invoices in that environment.
    • If you do not wish to enable Junior Dimensioning, select Continue without Junior Dimensioning. Junior will not be enabled and Procountor will not suggest enabling it. However, the feature can be enabled later in the Usage settings.
    • If the window is closed by clicking the X in the top right corner, the suggestion will not be displayed again. The suggestion will be displayed to the other users on the purchase invoice Verification view.

 

Enabling Junior Dimensioning on the Usage settings view:

  • If the above-mentioned conditions are met, Junior Dimensioning can also be enabled on the Usage settings view (Management > Company info > Usage settings).
  • Junior Dimensioning is enabled on the Usage settings view by selecting the option Use Junior dimension predictions in purchase invoices.
    • This enables Junior for all the suppliers and all purchase invoices in that environment.

 

In what kind of situations Junior Dimensioning is recommended to be enabled?

Situations where enabling Junior Dimensioning is recommended:

  • Enabling Junior Dimensioning is recommended if the expected accuracy for Junior’s dimension predictions in that certain environment is excellent. The expected accuracy is displayed in the guided setup when Junior dimensioning is enabled on the Verification -view.
  • Junior dimensioning can be of considerable help and is worth trying even if the expected accuracy is moderate. If Junior dimensioning is enabled with moderate expected accuracy, it may be wise to monitor how accurately Junior can predict the dimensions.

Situations where Junior Dimensioning might not be of additional help:

  • If default dimensions are effectively used in the environment, there may not be any additional benefit from using Junior dimensioning. In this case, it is recommended to keep using these Dimensions.

Things to consider when implementing Junior Dimensioning:

  • Junior dimensioning may not necessarily be able to make dimension predictions if the company has undergone changes in the past year in their dimension practices.  Junior will learn to predict more accurate suggestions in a couple of months.
    • Junior learns to make more accurate predictions even if it is not enabled in the Procountor environment.

 

What is the working logic of Junior Dimensioning?

Junior Dimensioning's Dimension predictions

Junior Dimensioning makes dimension predictions that are certain based on Junior's working logic, but also predictions that are uncertain based on its working logic.

  • When Junior Dimensioning is enabled in the Procountor environment, the fields that are highlighted with yellow background on invoice's Verification view are uncertain predictions, so those fields should be especially considered when reviewing Junior's predictions.
  • The fields on which Junior Dimensioning has made certain predictions based on its working logic, have not been highlighted. Even though Junior Dimensioning's working logic considers the prediction certain, it is still a prediction.
  • Junior Dimensioning's dimension predictions are created when the purchase invoice is created, or when the purchase invoice arrives to Procountor.
    • If a large number of purchase invoice is imported to Procountor through API interface, there may be a small delay in creation of the predictions.
    • Also, the dimension predictions are re-created, if the dimensioning of the invoice is edited, for example by editing the row info on the Invoice view.
  • Dimension predictions are not available if there is too many rows on the invoice. The limit is 300 rows.

 

Reviewing and handling of Junior Dimensioning's dimension predictions

  • Junior Dimensioning's predictions can be approved with Approve uncertain dimensions button, if the predictions seem to be correct, when reviewing the Verification view of the invoice.
  • If there is need to make corrections to Junior Dimensioning's predictions, the corrections can be made normally to the fields. After making the corrections, they must be saved with the Save button.
  • If Junior Dimensioning's dimension predictions are wanted to be disabled for one invoice it can be done on Verification view with the Junior dimension predictions switch. The same switch can be used for enabling Junior Dimensioning's  predictions for the invoice.
    • If Junior Dimensioning's predictions are switched off, the invoice's dimensioning will go according to dimension defaults.
    • If Junior Dimensioning's predictions are switched off, all color highlights regarding to the feature will vanish from the Verification view.
  • It should be taken into consideration, that if the row information on the Invoice view is edited after the dimension predictions have been reviewed and handled, Junior Dimensioning will make new predictions based on the new row information.

 

Dimensions view

In the Dimensions -view of the invoice, information is displayed on the top if dimension predictions have been made by Junior Dimensioning in that invoice. 

 

Accounting view

The Accounting view shows information if dimensions predictions have been made by Junior Dimensioning in that invoice.

 

Splitting dimension item in equal percentages

Junior Dimensioning cannot predict percentage allocation to items.  If there are more than one item, the feature will split dimension item in equal percentages. This can be changed in the usage settings by deselecting the Enable Junior to split dimension items in equal percentages -box.

 

Special situations

Special situations on invoice's Verification view

  • Junior Dimensioning's dimension predictions are created when the purchase invoice is created, or when the purchase invoice arrives to Procountor. If a large number of purchase invoice is imported to Procountor through API interface, there may be a small delay in creation of the predictions.
  • If the user edits dimensions before Junior Dimensioning gives its predictions, Junior Dimensioning will not "overwrite" edits made by the user.
  • Junior Dimensioning is not ready with the dimension predictions.
    • The Junior dimension predictions switch is disabled (cannot be used) and the dimensions are according to the dimension defaults.
  • Junior Dimensioning has been unsuccessful to give the predictions
    • The Junior dimension predictions switch is disabled (cannot be used) and the dimensions are according to the dimension defaults.
  • The tracking period or financial year has been closed before Junior Dimensioning has given its dimension predictions.
    • The dimensions on the closed tracking periods or financial years  will not be changed. The feature will not "overwrite" edits made by the user.
  • The Accounting by row selection has been unselected on the invoice's Invoice view.
    • Accounting by row must be enabled on the invoice and in the environment in order to use Junior Dimensioning.
  • Rows to transactions / Transactions to rows buttons have been used on the Accounting view of the invoice.
    • After this Junior Dimension’s predictions are no longer available for the invoice. Predictions are available again if the invoice's row info is edited and accounting of the invoice is created again. 

Dimensioning has been created for the invoice through the integration or through the import data.

  • Junior Dimensioning does not make dimension predictions if dimensioning has been created for the invoice through the integration or through the import data.

 

Receipt search

Receipts can be searched with different kinds of Junior Dimensioning-related search criteria on the Receipt search view. The search criteria related to Junior Dimensioning can be added in the Advanced search section of the view. After setting the search criteria, the receipts can be normally searched by clicking on the Search invoices button. 

 

How can Junior dimensioning be disabled in the Procountor environment?

Junior Dimensioning can be disabled by removing the selection from the Use Junior dimension predictions in purchase invoices setting on Usage settings view.

Please note, even if the Junior Dimensioning is disabled, the dimension predictions made by the feature will remain in accounting with those invoices where they are part of the saved dimensioning. Uncertain predictions are not highlighted anymore, and the Junior dimension predictions switch and other functions related to Junior Dimensioning is not in use.

We recommend that you review the uncertain predictions before disabling the feature.

articles.name: Credit invoice allocation
articles.title: Credit invoice allocation
articles.body:
You can search for credit notes by selecting Search > Credit note search on the left-hand side of the page. From this view you can allocate credit invoices to purchase invoices and search allocation payment lists.

 

Credit note search

Search criteria

By default, the program searches for purchase invoices that have fallen due by earliest a month ago (for example, if the current date is October 18th, the program will search for invoices where due date is by earliest September 18th).

You can filter the search criteria as follows:

  • Search: Search invoices based on name or invoice number, for example.
    • The search covers multiple invoice-related fields, such as name, address, products included on the invoice, and invoice number. You can search for multiple invoice numbers by placing a comma between the numbers (for example: "1, 2, 3") or by entering a range of numbers (such as "1–3").
  • Invoice date between: Search for invoices with an invoice date falling between specific dates.
  • Due date between: Search for invoices with a due date falling between specific dates.
  • Status: Select either all invoice statuses or filter the list.
    • Only the statuses in use can be selected.
  • Use the Select business partner button to search for the purchase invoices of a specific business partner. 
  • The Clear button resets the search criteria.

 

Search results

1. By activating the Show only credit invoices slide toggle, you can filter the search results to only show credit invoices.

2. Use the Go to button to see the Invoice or accounting view of the selected invoice or browse the attachments added to the invoice.

3. By clicking on the header of the column, you can sort the search results in a rising or falling order.

  • The button on the right-hand side of the search results (Toggle column visibility) allows you to adjust the visibility of the columns.
    • The button opens a list of columns that are displayed in the search results by default and enables you to hide a column from the search results by clicking it on the list.
  • The button on the left-hand side of the previous button (Reset default table settings) enables you to make any hidden columns visible in the search results, in other words display the default search results.

4. Use the Credit invoice allocation button to allocate invoices.

 

Allocate credit invoices

Unallocated invoices

You can allocate invoices by first selecting the supplier's invoice in the Search results and then selecting Credit invoice allocation. A supplier must be specified on the invoice.

The Credit invoice allocation view will open and you will see a default list of all the invoices from the supplier in question with the status Approved. The view lists the invoices from one supplier at a time.

By default, the program will only display the purchase invoices with the status Approved. You can adjust the search criteria. Only the invoices with the status Approved can be allocated. In other words, you cannot allocate invoices with the status Paid or Payment sent to bank, for example. 

How to allocate credit invoices:

1. Select at least one purchase invoice and one credit invoice that you wish to allocate. 

  • Credit invoices are allocated to purchase invoices according to their due date. If the selected credit is already allocated to invoices with an earlier due date in full, you will not be able to select invoices with a later due date to the group of allocated invoices.
  • The amount due calculated based on the invoices has to be equal or more than 0,00.

2. Click on the Allocate button.

3. The program will list the invoices to be allocated. You can edit the payment dates of individual invoices or set the same payment date for all the invoices. 

4. Click on the Allocate button. The invoices are allocated, their status is changed to Marked paid and they are transferred to the Allocated invoices view. If there are any amounts due in the allocation group, they are formed into a payment list about which you can learn more here.

  • Purchase invoices in different currencies cannot be allocated.
  • The button on the right-hand side closes the view and you return back to the Credit invoice search view .

 

Allocated invoices

In the Allocate credit notes view, select Allocated invoices to view the allocated invoices of the selected supplier.

You can search for allocation groups according to dates or date of allocation. You can only search for invoices with statuses of Payment queued, Payment sent to bank, Partly paid, Paid or Marked paid. Allocated invoices can only have one of these statuses.

  • The search result will display the most recent allocations first. 

  1. An allocation group consists of invoices that are allocated to each other. The date of the group shows when the invoices were allocated.
  2. You can hide and open invoices in the allocation group by clicking on the arrow in front of the group or selecting Show all or Hide all on the top row.
  3. By clicking on an invoice in an allocation group and selecting Invoice, accounting or attachments in the Go to button, you can see the details of an individual invoice. 
  • The button on the right-hand side closes the view and you return back to the Credit invoice search view .

 

Revert allocation

You can cancel the allocation by selecting Revert allocation. You cannot revert an allocation if the status of the purchase invoice is Payment queued, Payment sent to bank or Paid. 

You can revert the allocation if the status of all the invoices in the allocation group is Partly paid or Marked paid.

When you revert an allocation, the invoices in the allocation group are returned to Unallocated invoices and the Marked paid status is removed from the invoices.

 

Allocating of cash discounted invoices

If a full credit invoice is allocated to a purchase invoice where a cash discount is used, the allocation should only be done on the original due date of the invoice. If the allocation is made before the original due date of the invoice, while the cash discount is in use, the cash discount invoice will have a minus balance that cannot be edited. 

 

Allocation payment list search

When you have allocated the invoices and there are still payables remaining in the payment list after the allocation, a payment list is created. The Allocation payment list search on the top row allows you to process the payment lists. 

The Allocation payment list search view lists all the payment lists created in the environment. By default, the search results show the payment lists that have fallen due by earliest a month ago (for example, if the current date is October 18th, the program will search for payment lists where due date is by earliest September 18th).

By default, the program shows the payment lists with statuses Payment queued, Payment sent to bank, Partly paid, Paid or Marked paid. 

You can edit the search criteria by searching for payment lists by due date or payment date or selecting invoices with a specific status.

  • Click on the number of a payment list or activate a payment list row and select Payment list information to access the information of an individual payment list.

1. The Payment list view opens. The view is the same as the purchase invoice Payment view. 

2. You can see the open, unpaid sum of the payment list. You can edit the payment information, such as account number, sum or payment date. The view functions similarly to the purchase invoice Payment view.

3. The section Allocated invoices list shows all the invoices on the payment list. Click on the invoice number to view individual invoices. You can also pay the open sum in the view of an individual purchase invoice. 

4. In the Payment list view, you can pay the open sum by selecting Pay. You can also set the status of the payment as Marked paid. The payment is given the status Payment queued. The same information is also updated in the Payment view of the individual purchase invoice. At this point, the payment can still be canceled using the Cancel payment button.

5. The Delete payment list button allows you to delete the allocation of invoices in a chosen payment list. The Marked paid entry is removed from the purchase invoices and the invoices are returned to the Unallocated invoices listing in the Allocate credit notes view.

  • A payment list cannot be deleted if the status of a purchase invoice in the payment list is Payment queued, Payment sent to bank or Paid. 
  • Payment transactions cannot be deleted from the payment list. Deleting the Marked paid payment transaction of allocated invoices is not possible.
    • If you wish to delete the payment transaction of an allocated invoice, this must be carried out in the Allocated invoices view.
  • The button on the right-hand side closes the view and you return back to the Allocation payment list search view .

 

Information coming with payable invoices

The invoices to be paid include additional information about invoices that are assigned to each other, i.e. information whether the invoice is a credit or debit invoice and the original amounts of the invoices.

Additional information is currently only included in SEPA payments, and it depends on the receiving bank does the bank process the additional information or not. If the information is processed and forwarded by the bank, the above-mentioned information will appear in the account transaction of the recipient.

 

Purchase invoice view

When you allocate purchase invoices, they form an allocation group and a separate payment list if there are payables remaining in the allocation group.

The Invoice view of the purchase invoice display the section Credit invoice allocation. 

The section displays all the invoices to which the purchase invoice is allocated and the number of the possible payment list. 

  • If you wish to go to the Invoice view of another invoice in the allocation group, click on the invoice in question.
    • The program opens the other invoice in a new tab.
  • Click on the number of the payment list to access the Payment list. 
    • The payment list opens in a new tab.
    • If any payables remain in the payment list, you can pay the open sum in the Payment list view or an individual purchase invoice in the Payment view.

articles.name: Sales reporting
articles.title: Sales reporting
articles.body:
You can access the sales report in Reporting > Sales reporting. The reporting system retrieves the information in real time from Procountor's database. 

Sales reports help you monitor sales according to products and customers. 

 

User rights

In order for the user to view the sales report, they must have at least the following user rights:

  • Search sales invoices: Viewing rights or All rights
  • No limitation in use: Access only sales invoices created by user
  • No additional feature in use: Dimension-specific limitation

 

Search criteria

  1. First, define the search criteria for the report.
  2. Click Apply.
  3. The program generates sales reports in line with the search criteria.

The report can be filtered with the following criteria:

 

Time Period

  • Current period
  • Last 6 months
  • Last 12 months
  • Current year
  • Custom period
    • Start and End: Free date definition either by filling values in the fields or by using the calendar icon. 
    • The data of the report is retrieved from sales invoices by default by invoice date.

 

Products

The Product button opens the product selection. You can search for products, product groups and invoice products.

  • Products: The section displays all the products entered into the product register, regardless of whether they have been used in invoices.
  • Product groups: The section displays the sales product groups used to search for products in said product group.
  • Invoice products: The section only displays the products used in invoices. The product does not have to be set up in the product register.

Search field: You can filter the list by entering any part of the name of products, product groups and invoice products. It is also possible to search products by the product code.

 

Customers

The Customer button opens the customer selection. You can search for customers, customer groups and invoice customers.

  • Customers: The section displays all the customers who have been entered in the customer register.
  • Customer groups: The section displays the customer groups used to search for sales in said customer group.
  • Invoice customers: The section displays only the customers with a registered invoice. The customer does not have to be set up in the customer register.

Search field: You can filter the list by entering the name or the first few characters of the customer, customer group or invoice customer.

It is also possible to search customers and invoice customers by the customer number.

 

Figures

  • EUR: sales in EUR excluding value added tax (the name of the button is according to the currency of the country of the Procountor's environment).
  • EUR + VAT: sales in EUR inluding value added tax (the name of the button is according to the currency of the country of the Procountor's environment).
  • Quantity: number of products in sales invoices.

 

Invoice date or receipt date

  • You can choose whether to search for sales invoices according to invoice date or receipt date.

 

Transactions

  • All transactions: searches for both business transactions and other transactions.
  • Business transactions: searches for business transactions, in other words receipts with the status Not sent, Approved, Sent, Paid, Partly paid, Marked paid or Invoiced.
  • Others transactions: searches for other than business transactions. 

 

Create report

Apply makes the program search for information in line with the search criteria.

Reset to default clears your selections and resets the default search criteria.

 

View details

View details allows you to browse the content of the graphs at row level.

With a  pivot table you can group sales data and easily spot trends and patterns. The pivot displays the sales information based on the reports general filters, and can be optimized to many options. 
 
You can group sales invoice rows based on Product, Product groups, Customer, Customer groups, Invoice customer and Invoice product. Sales are summarized on either yearly, monthly or daily basis depending on the time range applied. 
 
On the view you can at the same time view the individual sales invoice rows in the table below for full insight into the data. 

  • The Export to excel –button exports the report data to an Excel file.
  • The Table can be expanded or minimized with the icon. 

 

Sales overview

The topmost graph presents the general sales development in line with the search criteria. 

You can track the development of sales per year, month or day, for example. In the drop-down menu of the Show button, select one of the following:

  • Yearly
  • monthly
  • daily
  • weekly

You can select various graph types. In the Graph type drop-down menu, select one of the following:

  • Periodic 
  • Cumulative development of sales 
  • Comparison of sales with previous year 
  • Comparison of cumulative sales with previous year 
  • Changing rate of sales from previous year 

The graph can be saved as a PNG-format image file by clicking on the Export to PNG button. 

 

Sales by product, product group and invoice product

The middle graph in the view examines the sales at the product level.

Filtering the information

  • On the header row of the graph, you can select whether to browse the graph per product, product group or invoice product. 
    • On the Product -tab, sales are displayed listed according to the products in the product register.
    • On the Invoice products -tab, sales are displayed according to the products entered on the invoices. The tab shows the products that have not been added to the product register or the product name differs from the product name in the register.
  • You can change the results of the graph in a rising or falling order by clicking on the arrow next to the column.
  • In the table, you can choose to view a product, a product group or an invoice product by clicking on the product's name, for example. Reselect the same row to reset the filters.

Buttons

  • The Export to excel –button exports the table data to an Excel file.
  • The Table can be expanded or minimized with the icon. 
  • From the button, you can drill down from product table to invoices, so that you can see which invoices are related to chosen product.
    • From the Invoices’ view, it is possible to drill down to the individual invoice by clicking the invoice number. 

 

Sales by customer, customer group and invoice customer

The bottom graph in the view examines sales at customer level. 

Filtering the information

  • On the header row of the graph, you can select whether to browse the graph per customer, customer group or invoice customer.
    • On the Customers - tab, sales are displayed listed according to the customers in the Procountor's customer register.
    • On the Invoice customers -tab, sales are displayed according to the customers appearing on the invoices. The tab shows the sales invoices of customers who have not been added to the customer register or whose name differs from the name in the register.
  • You can change the results of the graph to a rising or falling order by clicking on the arrow next to the column.
  • In the table, you can choose to view a customer, a customer group or an invoice customer by clicking on the customer's name, for example. Reselect the same row to reset the filters.

Buttons

  • The Export to excel –button exports the table data to an Excel file.
  • The Table can be expanded or minimized with the icon. 
  • From the button, you can drill down from customer table to invoices, so that you can see which invoices are related to chosen customer.
    • From the Invoices’ view, it is possible to drill down to the individual invoice by clicking the invoice number.

articles.name: Personal information
articles.title: Personal information
articles.body: Via the Menu button in the lower right corner and selecting Personal information (own name)  -view, you can see your user information such as your username, email address and phone number. The data comes from browser version of Procountor, where you can modify it if necessary.

articles.name: Procountor mobile app
articles.title: Procountor mobile app
articles.body:
What is Procountor mobile?

The Procountor Mobile App is a modern, user-friendly extension of the Procountor financial management solution, designed to save you time and streamline your financial tasks.

With Procountor Mobile, you can manage receipts, create and approve travel, expense and purchase invoices, and send sales invoices, all within the same easy-to-use application. 

Download Procountor from the App Store or Google Play and experience the convenience of managing your finances on the go.

  • Procountor mobile works on iOS and Android mobile devices.
  • For Procountor Financials customers.
  • You can customize the application to your needs. Select the functions you need in your daily life. The verification and approval of invoices and the invoice archive are free features.
  • Information is updated in real time between the Procountor mobile application and the Procountor software.
  • The application helps in filling in the information and guides in various functions.
  • Available in Finnish, in Swedish and in English.

 

Pricing

  • The application can be downloaded free of charge from app stores.
  • The free features are the verification and approval of invoices.
  • Features that are subject to a charge are the creation of travel, expense, purchase and sales invoices, taking photographs of receipts and payment functions. These features can be activated directly in the application.
  • The price of the environment is EUR 8.49/month/user. The price is added to the company’s Procountor invoice.

 

Activation of paid Features

The use of paid features must be approved separately within the app.
When you navigate to a paid feature, such as receipts, the app will prompt you to activate paid features.

  • If you wish to enable paid features, press Activate Paid Features.
  • If you do not want to enable the features, select No thanks, hide this. This will hide the feature from the app.
    • However, you can still enable paid features later via the Menu section of the app.
  • If the activation of paid features is restricted in the company settings, the app will notify you separately. You can read more about allowing or restricting the use of paid features here.

 

Logging in

  1. Search for "Procountor" in your application store: App Store and Google Play.
  2. Download the application
  3. Log into Procountor mobile using your existing Procountor ID and personal password.
  4. After logging in, you are all set!
     

 

Features

Once you have logged into the Procountor app, you can use its functions. The links below will take you directly to the instructions for each function. The app will also guide you when you use a function for the first time.

Please note that your organization may have restricted the use of paid features, in which case the paid features will not be available. If needed, you can contact your Procountor admin or accountant about this.

  • Verify and approve invoices
  • Take pictures of receipts
  • Create expense invoices
  • Create travel invoices
  • Create purchase invoices
  • Create and send sales invoices
  • Pay invoices

 

Support

Procountor Customer Service is happy to help you with questions relating to the use of the Procountor mobile.

Contact form

(Tickets are handled Mon-Fri between 8 am and 4 pm)

You can also find Procountor mobile instructions directly in the application.

articles.name: Creating travel invoice
articles.title: Creating travel invoice
articles.body:
1. Start by tapping on the Travel button on the homepage or by tapping on the Trips button in the sub-menu. In the My travels view, tap on New travel.

2. Trip details: Enter the information of the trip, such as trip purpose and destination, start and end dates.

  • These affect the calculations of the daily allowance.
  • Proceed by clicking the Next button or by swiping the screen.

3. Trip abroad: Activate the Did you travel abroad? toggle button if you traveled abroad during your trip.

  • Enter the details of your international trip.
  • The information will affect the calculation of the daily allowance.
  • Proceed by clicking the Next button or by swiping the screen.

4. Daily allowance: The application has calculated the daily allowance according to the duration of the trip.

  • You can add day-specific information, such as meal compensation, by tapping on the day of travel.
  • Finally, press Done.

5. Kilometer allowance: If you used your own vehicle during the trip, press the Add Trip button.

  • Select the vehicle you used and add any extra passengers.
  • Enter the route of the trip.
    • The application has automatic completion for the start and end points of the trip and calculates the route length.
  • You can also add waypoints to the route by pressing the +Add waypoint button at the bottom.
  • Finally, press Done.

6. Expenses: If you paid with own money work-related expenses during the trip, enter them here by pressing the +Add expense button.

  • If they are expenses paid abroad, please note that the invoice is generated in EUR. The program will use the exchange rate specified in Procountor.
  • Finally, press Done.

7. Summary: You will see a summary of your trip.

  • You can go back to correct the information if necessary.

8. Finish by tapping Done. You can save the invoice as unfinished or you can save and send it to circulation.

  • When the travel invoice is sent to circulation, it is marked waiting for verification in the application. The travel invoice is transferred to the Procountor software with the status Received. 
  • If the invoice is saved as unfinished, you can find it under Unfinished heading in the Travels -section.

9. The invoice must first be verified and approved before it can be paid.

articles.name: Photographing receipts
articles.title: Photographing receipts
articles.body:
1. Start by tapping on the Receipt button on the homepage or by selecting Receipts > New receipt in the sub-menu.
  2. Take a picture of the receipt. Use the Flashlight in the top corner if you are taking the picture in low light.
    You can also search for receipt stored in the phone's photo gallery by pressing the Photos icon in the lower right corner.
    From the Documents icon in the lower left corner, you can retrieve receipts stored in the phone's own files.
  3. Mobile tries to recognize the edges of the receipt and borders the receipt automatically. You can modify the cropping area if you want. 
  4. Tap on the Done button or you can take a new picture by pressing Retake. 
  5. Procountor will read the information on the receipt and enter it automatically. You can add the information of only one receipt at a time. You can add other attachments to the receipt by pressing New attachment -button.
  6. You can manually edit the information recognized by Procountor in the application and later in Procountor. Mandatory information are payment method, purchase date, amount and VAT%. Select the Payment method for the receipt:
    1. Company credit card
    2. Company debit card
    3. Company cash
    4. Company bank transfer
    5. Paid with own money
      • The mobile automatically creates a new expense invoice from the receipt. If you have an expense invoice that is in progress, the application adds a receipt to that invoice.
      • Please remember to send the invoice when it is ready.
  7. Tap on the Done button. The receipt is saved in the application and transferred to the Cost receipts management section of the Procountor software for processing.

The maximum size of the file is 10mb.

articles.name: Users and user rights
articles.title: Users and user rights
articles.body:
In the Users and user rights -view, you can specify the user rights of different users in the organization’s Procountor environment. You can also add new users to the Procountor environment and remove users from the environment.

This article explains how you can search for users based on their privileges, specify privileges for them and examine the user right change log. 

 You can find the view by selecting Management > Users and user rights in the main menu.

  • All users with viewing rights to the Users and user rights section can access the view.
  • Editing privileges and browsing the user right change log require All rights to the Users and user rights section. 

 

Searching users

You can search for users in the environment under Management > Users and privileges.

By default, the Procountor groups users by their user roles. You can remove the grouping clicking on the button next to the Group by user roles text.

 

Searching users by privileges

  1. First, select the privilege you wish to use as the search criterion on the user right drop-down menu.
  2. In the Access drop-down menu, specify which right the user must have to the privilege.
  3. The program automatically lists the users who meet your search criterion in the All users section

  • You can select multiple privileges as your search criteria. The program automatically adds the new search criterion under the previous ones.
  • To remove a search criterion, click on the cross button next to the criterion.
  • Click on the Clear all filters criteria button to remove all your search criteria.

 

Editing User rights

  1. When you select a user on the left-hand side column, the user’s rights open on the right-hand side column.
  2. You can select an existing role for the user that will determine their user rights or you can specify individual user rights by selecting one of the following in the right-hand side drop-down menu of the privilege in question
  • All rights
  • Viewing rights
  • No access

3. Save your changes by clicking on Save at the top.

Changing a user’s privileges within one Procountor environment will not affect their privileges in other environments in which they have access rights. 

Please note

  • Some of the user rights are mutually exclusive. The program will automatically prevent selecting access rights that would conflict with existing privileges.
  • If an user right is related to a limitation, a question mark is shown after it. To see what the limitation applies to, hover your mouse on top of the question mark.
  • The user rights related to the retrieval of purchase, travel and expense invoices and journal receipts are interrelated and cannot be specified separately. For example, if you grant a user all rights to search purchase invoices , the program automatically gives all rights to search and view travel and expense invoices and journal receipts.

 

User right limitations

Limitations are disabled by default, but they can be enabled to provide users with privileges that are more extended than those of the Personnel role, but more limited than full privileges.

Limitations appear under the group to which the user rights relates. For more information about the effect of the limitation, hover your mouse over the question mark next to it.

For example, you can grant user privileges to create and edit his or her own travel and expense invoices by selecting the option Access only travel & expense invoices created by user and by granting the user full rights to the Rights for travel & expense invoices and Search travel & expense invoices.  

 

Copying user rights

You can also copy a user’s rights to other user(s).

  1. Select all the users to whom you wish to copy the rights in the Users column and the user whose rights you wish to copy.
  2. The users you selected in the Users column will appear in the User rights column on the right.
  3. Next, select the user whose access rights you wish to copy by checking the box in front of their name. Click on the Copy rights button to copy the user’s rights.
  4. Select the users to whom you wish to copy the rights and click on Paste rights.

 

Printing user information

To convert the names of environment users to printable form, right-click on the user list and select Export list of selected users, Excel, HTML or PDF.

You can convert the User rights to printable form by clicking on Export in the User rights section and selecting either Export Excel, Export HTML or Open PDF in the drop-down menu. 

The file includes the information of all the selected users.

 

User change log

You can access the User change log from the top menu of the Users and user right -view.

The User change log -view is only accessible to users with all rights to the users and user rights -section.

The change log shows all the changes made to the user’s privileges in the selected environment. You can also browse the privileges of deleted users.

The change log shows a summary of the change, i.e., when the privilege was changed, which user’s information was changed, what the action was and who made the change.

  • The user change log can be exported in PDF, Excel or HTML format. Start by selecting the users whose data you wish to export and click on the Export PDF, Export HTML or Export Excel button at the top

You can see all the changes made to a user’s access rights by clicking on their name. The old value shows what the user’s previous user rights were, and the new value indicates the user’s new user rights. 

  • The change log can be exported in PDF, Excel or HTML format.

 

User roles

Procountor includes the following preset roles for defining user rights:

  • Accountant
  • Employee
  • Entrepreneur
  • Main user
  • Management / Auditor
  • Payment transactions
  • Payroll accountant
  • Purchases
  • Sale
  • Student

When a role has been assigned to a user, the preset rights appear to the user right view. The related user rights can be edited as desired (with the exception of the Personnel role).

If you want to customize your own set of user rights to the user, user's role changes into Customised role. This role will automatically modify the users rights as No rights and after this the users rights should be modifies to grant the user some visibility in Procountor.

Only the functions to which a user has privileges are visible to him or her in the main menu.

You should only give full user management rights to the main user and his or her substitute.

 

General information about the Main user role

The main user of the environment has rights to all functions of the environment by default. The main user can, for example, edit basic company info, add new users and edit user roles. The main user can also see all salary functions and employee’s salary information. The main user role can also be edited and user rights to different functions can be modify.

 

General information about the Employee role

Employee users only have rights to create travel and expense invoices for themselves, search for their own travel and expense invoices in the system, and view their own salary information. The Employee role cannot be modified. Before a Employee user can create travel and expense invoices, that user’s social security number must be saved in complete form into the user’s personal information and the company’s Business partner register, in which the user is registered as a Person.

If the user sees an error message when trying to prepare a travel or expense invoice, check that the user’s social security number is entered in Personal information and settings and the users username is attached to the person in Person register. If the user is still unable create travel or expense invoices, this means that the personal information is missing from the person register. Please contact your company’s main user if you need to supplement your information in the person register.

By default, users with the Employee role are prevented from editing dimensions. If you want to create a user with the Employee role permissions but also allow dimension editing, you can select another role (for example, Customized) and assign exactly the same user rights as the default Employee role. This way, dimension editing will also be possible.

 

User roles of Solo product version

User roles of Solo product version differ from the user roles of Financials and Ledger product versions in the following way:
