  • If the "invoiceApprovalInformation" element is left blank in the API request: {}, approvers and verifiers are not set on the invoice at all, regardless of the environment settings or any defaults.

 

Endpoints to be used and other requirements

 

GET ​/company​/invoicecirculation​/settings endpoint returns the circulation settings of the Procountor environment. 

GET ​/company​/invoicecirculation​/verifierlists endpoint returns the verifier lists, if created in the Procountor environment

GET ​/company​/invoicecirculation​/verifierlists​/{id} endpoint returns a separate list of verifiers, if created.

Setting of verifiers and approvers to purchase invoice in API request does not require any verifiers lists in Procountor, but verifiers can be set also without lists. But note, that it is not easy to retrieve ids of the all users through the API interface.

articles.name: Procountor Finago Kassaturva
articles.title: Procountor Finago Kassaturva
articles.body:
What is Finago Kassaturva?

Finago Kassaturva is an agile service that allows you to finance your receivables of any size. This way, you get the money from your sales invoices immediately into your account for handling purchases, salaries, taxes, and other expenses. With this service, you can choose when and how much financing you use, and the only cost is the commission charged on the financed receivables.

Finago Kassaturva is integrated with Procountor and it helps the handling of sales invoices through the API interface. The service is suitable for financing receivables from corporate customers (business ID) and foreign customers. The service is implemented in collaboration with our partner Alisa pankki Oyj and is available directly from Procountor.

Learn more about the Finago Kassaturva service and order it here (in Finnish).

 

Implementation

  1. Make an agreement with Alisa Bank for the use of Finago Kassaturva. Order the service here. Alisa Bank will process the order and you will receive the service agreement for signing. If you have sent all the necessary information to the bank, you will get access to Finago Kassaturva on the same day or within a few days.
  2. After making an agreement with Alisa pankki Oyj for Finago Kassaturva, activate the external financing services in Procountor under Management > Company Information > Usage Settings > Is external financing in use?
  3. Add the technical user ID for Finago Kassaturva to Procountor according to the instructions from Alisa pankki (instructions in the email sent by Alisa pankki ).
  4. Check that the chart of accounts has the necessary accounts for implementing external financing. Contact your accountant if needed. Instructions for the necessary changes in accounting can be found below.
  5. After this, confirm to Alisa pankki via email that the changes have been made. After confirmation, we will automatically fill in the Finago Kassaturva financing agreement details in Procountor under Management > Company Information > Financing Agreements.
  6. From now on, you can finance your receivables with Finago Kassaturva. Read more about using external financing here.

 

Changes to be made in accounting

  1. During implementation, ensure that the chart of accounts includes the accounts 1718 Receivables, financing, 2842 Short-term debt, and 9640 Financing costs (otherwise the functions performed through the API will not work).

  2. Create a new default posting rule for the bank statement. The default posting rule can possibly be made, for example, based on the name Alisa Bank Oyj, if the receivables financed by Finago Kassaturva always appear on the bank statement in this way. More information on creating default postings can be found here. The default account would be the aforementioned 2842.

    For Finago Kassaturva customers opened after 8 December 2025, payments will be credited using the standard reference. Create a new default posting rule for reference-based payments. The default posting rule can possibly be created, for example, based on the name “Alisa Bank oyj” or by using the standard reference indicated in the email sent by Alisa Bank. More information on creating a default posting rule can be found here. The default account to be set would be the 2842.

  3. For customers whose invoices are selected for financing, a new default account 1718 Receivables, financing must be defined. This way, the posting of financed invoices will be automated in the future.
    1. Financed customers can be retrieved in bulk from the Business Partner Report by selecting the account number and Finago Kassaturva’s financing account number as the search criteria. The account number can be checked from the Financing Agreements view.

 

Using the financing agreement on invoices

In a situation where all invoices from a certain supplier are financed, the agreement can be added as a default behind the customer in the program under Registers > Customer Register > Select Customer > Financing Agreement. After this, the Finago Kassaturva financing agreement will be automatically selected for all new invoices of the customer.

  • You can also add agreements in bulk to multiple customers under Registers > Customer Register > Edit Multiple > Retrieve Business Partners and select the ones to be edited > Edit Business Partners > Financing Agreement.
  • We recommend informing the accountant of the customers whose invoices are financed with Finago Kassaturva. This way, the accountant can respond to the default posting changes of the receivables.

The invoice is sent to the customer in the usual way from Procountor after pressing the Send button.

Read more about using the financing agreement here.

 

Special notes regarding Finago Kassaturva financing agreements

  • The Finago Kassaturva financing agreement can also be used on consumer customer invoices. This feature is not activated automatically for consumer customer invoices but must be agreed upon separately with Alisa pankki.
  • If an invoice is copied from an old invoice, it is particularly important that the financing agreement is added to the customer register before copying. During copying, select Original in the Business Partner field, retrieve the information from the register so that the changed register information is transferred to the new invoice.
  • Financing agreements can also be used only on certain invoices. We recommend that financing agreements be used consistently on all invoices of a certain customer so that the receiving system of the customer keeps up with the account number of the payable invoice.

 

Sending financing data to Alisa pankki

Information about the invoice to be financed is sent to Alisa pankki when the invoice is in Sent status. After this, the invoice can no longer be returned to In Progress status and it has been sent to both the customer and Alisa pankki for financing. The financing data is sent using the API interface and the sending happens automatically after pressing the Send button. A financed invoice can only be returned to the In progress status by customer service.

 

Financing and marking the invoice as paid

The invoice is financed according to the agreement made with Alisa pankki . The first remittance of the receivable appears on the bank statement at the earliest the next day. When the customer pays the invoice in full, the sales invoice is automatically marked as Paid Elsewhere. Alisa pankki charges financing costs in connection with the remitted receivables according to the financing agreement. During the final remittance, an automatic memo is created, which records the financing costs in the accounting. This memo shows which invoice(s) the financing concerns.

  • If you have multiple invoices to be financed, the invoices are remitted to the bank statement as a single transaction using the standard message (Finago Kassaturva).
  • If you have multiple invoices to be financed, they will be credited to the account statement as a single payment using the specified standard reference. For Finago Kassaturva customers opened after 8 December 2025, payments will be credited using the standard reference.

 

Accounting notes for marking the invoice as paid

The sales invoice is recorded as follows:

  • 1718 Receivables, financing / 3000 Sales

Payments received on the bank statement are posted as follows:

  • 1910 Bank Account / 2842 Short-term debt

Financing costs are automatically recorded monthly with a memo coming through the API:

  • 9640 Financing costs / 2842 Short-term debt

During the final payment, when the customer pays the invoice, Alisa pankki remits the remaining receivables on the bank statement and provides the final financing costs (if any) with a memo to Procountor.

  • 2842 Short-term debt / 1718 Receivables, financing
  • 1910 Bank Account / 2842 Short-term debt

After this, the accounting and ledger match.

 

Handling credit invoices

Credit invoices are created in the usual way and information about financed invoices is not separately provided to Alisa pankki . Alisa pankki retrieves credit invoices automatically from Procountor through the API interface.

articles.name: Set-up of Finago Procountor Solo: accountant's instructions
articles.title: Set-up of Finago Procountor Solo: accountant's instructions
articles.body:
This article describes the Finago Procountor Solo set-up process from the point of view of the accountant.

 

Set up a new environment view

The Finago Procountor Solo environment is set up in Procountor under Management > Set up a new environment.

  • Another option is to change the current Procountor environment into a Solo environment. The instructions can be found here.

1. Go to the Set up a new environment view.

2. Enter the information and select Finago Procountor Solo as the product version.

3. Select either Procountor default account scheme as the chart of accounts or copy the chart from another Solo environment.

Please note! It is very important to choose the correct chart of accounts when setting up a new environment since the chosen chart of accounts can't be changed after the environment has been created.

4. Select the product register. If you wish, you can copy the product register from an existing Solo environment or select the default register.

  • Copying the chart of accounts and product register from an existing Solo environment facilitates the set-up of new Solo environments.
    • Copying from an existing environment is recommended if you use a modified chart of accounts or purchases product register.
    • If you copy the chart of accounts from another environment, you must copy the product register from the same environment in order to keep the default posting settings.
    • More instructions on the importance of the product register are here. 
  • If you select the default chart of accounts, you can select either sole trader or limited liability as the product register template and Finnish or English as the language.
    • The differences between the product registers for sole traders and limited liability companies are:
      • The product register for sole traders includes the product "Private/own withdrawal", whereas the Ltd register has "Own purchase/shareholder loan"
      • The sole trader's register refers to the employee's salary, whereas for limited liability companies, the name is the entrepreneur's or employee’s salary

5. Copy the usage settings.

6. After setting up the environment, create a new username for the Solo entrepreneur or add the entrepreneur's existing username to the environment.

  • It is particularly important to add the entrepreneur with the user role Finago Procountor Solo entrepreneur so that they receive the login instructions for the Finago Procountor Solo user interface.
  • If you add an existing entrepreneur's username to the environment, you must ensure that the entrepreneur has added their phone number and e-mail address to their own information and settings. If this information has not been added, the login instructions cannot be sent to the entrepreneur.
  • You can only ad one entrepreneur with the Finago Procountor Solo entrepreneur role to the environment.
  • If the entrepreneur already has a username in Procountor financial management, they do not need a new username. They can use their existing username to log into Solo if the user role is changed into Finago Procountor Solo entrepreneur.
  • The Solo entrepreneur logs into the entrepreneur's user interface through the Solo login window. The Solo entrepreneur does not need the Procountor password list or confirmation through the Key application when they log in.
  • Solo entrepreneurs use the Key application to confirm payments in the Solo user interface. If the Solo entrepreneur's username is also linked to a Procountor Financials or Procountor Ledger environment, they can use the same Key smartphone application for confirming payments in the Solo user interface and logging into the Procountor environments. This can only be done if the username is the same in all of these environments – the Key application cannot be linked to several usernames at the same time.

 

Setting up privileges

The accountant and the entrepreneur must be given full privileges in the new Procountor environment. Management > Users and privileges. 

  • The Users and privileges view of Procountor must have at least two users: the entrepreneur and the accountant.

 

User roles

Accountant 

The accountant's user role is Accountant. 

  • The accountant who sets up the environment automatically receives privileges to the company's user management.
  • If several accountants or payroll accountants are added to the environment, at least one of the users must have User management privileges. 

Finago Procountor Solo entrepreneur 

The entrepreneur's user role is Finago Procountor Solo entrepreneur. 

  • When the user role is set up as Finago Procountor Solo entrepreneur, the program automatically sends the user an e-mail with a link to the Finago Procountor Solo login page. 
  • The entrepreneur only uses the Finago Procountor Solo entrepreneur's user interface, which means they do not log into the Procountor environment. By default, the Finago Procountor Solo entrepreneur's user rights do not allow logging into the Procountor user interface.
  • The entrepreneur uses their Procountor username to log into Finago Procountor Solo.

Payroll accountant

The payroll accountant can be given the Payroll accountant user role. 

  • If salaries are calculated with the help of Procountor salary calculation by a person other than the accountant, a payroll accountant's username can be added to the environment.  

Management/Auditor

The auditor can be given the Management/Auditor role. 

  • If the company is covered by the auditing obligation, it can complete the auditing electronically in the Finago Procountor Solo environment by adding the auditor's Procountor username to the environment.

Customized

If the aim is to customize the privileges manually, select Customized as the role. 

 

Setting up the bank connections

In order to use the full features of Finago Procountor Solo, the user's bank account must be linked to Finago Procountor Solo (in the accountant's user interface) so that the bank statements and reference payments arrive regularly from the bank. The entrepreneur must fill out the bank connection authorization that is sent to the bank. After this, when the bank has opened the bank connection, the accountant adds the company's bank account to the Procountor environment under Management > Company info > Bank account information.

Note! The bank account must be a company account in order to function in Procountor and the Solo entrepreneur's user interface. In general, banks cannot grant software companies the right to transmit payment data from a private person's bank account.

  • More detailed instructions on adding the bank account can be found here. 
  • The bank connection authorization forms are available here. 

 

Electronic invoice addresses

Procountor automatically activates the electronic invoice addresses. A prerequisite for activating the electronic invoice addresses is that we have processed the agreement and the environment is in production use. After this, the activation starts right away when the entrepreneur logs into Finago Procountor Solo. The activation normally takes approximately three working days.

Note! After the electronic invoice addresses have been activated and the account can be used, it takes approximately one week before the addresses are listed in the public https://verkkolaskuosoite.fi/ website.

  • The entrepreneur's electronic invoice addresses are not visible in the E-Invoice and Scanning provider addresses view in the accountant's Procountor environment. 

 

Managing the product register for purchases

The product register for purchases is managed in the Procountor environment, and this is visible in the Finago Procountor Solo entrepreneur's user interface. The entrepreneur uses the product register in Solo when they select the expense type for purchase invoices or receipts. It is recommended that you modify the product register based on the entrepreneur's business activities so that the entrepreneur has an easy-to-use list of expense types available in their own Solo user interface. The same product register can be copied to new Solo environments in the future. 

The product register can be found under Registers > Product register for purchases in the program.

You can add new products to the product register by clicking the Add product button. Use the Remove button to remove existing products from the register. Removed products cannot be restored, but you can create a new similar product, if necessary. You can also set the status of a product as passive in the product register. The entrepreneur sees all the purchase products set up in the product register in their Solo user interface.  

We recommend specifying the default posting of the products as accurately as possible to ensure smooth posting in the future. Expenses are recorded based on the default posting settings, and the entrepreneur allocates the expense to the correct product in the Solo user interface. Read more about the product register here.

 

Posting rules for received payments

The entrepreneur creates and sends sales invoices in the Finago Procountor Solo user interface. Each sales invoice sent by the entrepreneur has a bank reference code by default. When the end client pays the sales invoice using the bank reference code, the payment transaction appears on the reference payment list provided by the bank. 

In Procountor, the reference payment list creates a separate accounting page. The Finago Procountor Solo entrepreneur's accounting is cash-based, which means that the receivables are not handled and the sales are recorded in Procountor on the reference payment accounting page.

The VAT percentages, VAT statuses and accounting account (3000) of the sales invoices are sent from the Solo environment to Procountor with the accounting material, also when the sales invoice has several different VAT percentages. 

If you want to change the accounting account, you can make changes to the default posting of reference payments. This editing overrides the accounting account information imported from Finago Procountor Solo. Please note that this also works vice versa: if an entry is recorded on an account other than 3000, you should check the current default posting settings for reference payments.  See the detailed editing instructions here.

 

Beginning accounting in Procountor

You must make certain specifications in the Management menu in the new Procountor environment in order to begin accounting. 

 

Financial years

Financial years are set in Procountor under Management > Accounting info > Financial years.

Click the New fiscal year button create a new row and specify the start and end dates for the fiscal period. If you want to import the balance information of the previous financial year, you must also set up the previous financial year.

We also recommend setting up tracking periods for monitoring the financial year, as these enable closing the accounting monthly. You can manage tracking periods under Financial years > Edit tracking periods > Create tracking periods.  Read more on tracking periods here.

Finago Procountor Solo entrepreneurs submit accounting material to the environment monthly, which means the bank statements are also processed monthly. When the months accounting is ready and the own-initiative tax return has been sent, the tracking period for the month is closed. This protects the accounting against changes.

In Procountor, the Bank statements and reference payments view contains the Update accounting button, which can be used to edit the accounting pages of all the bank statements and reference payments in the view. By closing the tracking period, you can lock the accounts of previous months to avoid making changes to completed months with the Update accounting button. 

 

Taxation information

The Taxation information view specifies the duration of the company's VAT period and the Tax Account's reference and bank account number which are needed for creating the own-initiative tax return. The view also determines which income tax return form is used. In the Income tax return menu, select form 6B for companies and 5 for sole traders.  

Taxation information can be found in Procountor under Management > Accounting info > Taxation information.

 

VAT defaults

The VAT defaults view specifies which VAT statuses can be selected for the accounting entries. It is possible that all of the VAT statuses available in the program by default are not needed in the entrepreneur's accounting. You can customize the default settings so that only the VAT statuses that are needed in the accounting are active in the environment.

You cannot edit or disable the default VAT statuses or percentages, but you can lock the selections. Version upgrade v69 restored all previously edited values back to defaults.  

You can specify VAT defaults in Management > Accounting info > VAT defaults.

 

Transferring opening balances in accounting

When you start new accounting, you usually need to transfer comparison data and the balances for transactions in the previous financial year from the old accounts. More instructions on beginning accounting can be found here.

 

Other settings

Below are the most important settings options that need to considered when setting up Finago Procountor Solo. When you are setting up a Solo environment, you should also check the other general settings in Procountor in the Basic info and Usage settings views.

 

Dimension settings

Finago Procountor Solo has one dimension (cost centre) by default. This dimension can be named, and items can be set up under it in the Dimensions view, which can be found by selecting Management > Accounting info > Dimensions in the main menu. Dimensions can be set for bank statement transactions and receipts in Solo as in any other Procountor product. More information on dimensioning is available in this article.

 

Language settings

Via language settings, you can edit Solo so that your customer can use it in English. Regardless of the language set for your customer, you can continue using Procountor in your preferred language. Read more about the language settings and the changes they require: Switching the language of Finago Procountor Solo to English.

articles.name: Default postings for taxes
articles.title: Default postings for taxes
articles.body:
The default posting for taxes can be changed in Management > Accounting info > Posting defaults > Default postings for taxes. 

 

 

Default tax postings can be changed according to users wishers and the changes effect new invoices. This means that the changes should be taken into consideration when balancing. 

Taxes are divided in 3 different sections:

Default accounts for taxes


- Tax liability account
- Default account for withhold tax
- VAT liability account
- Account for payment based VAT

Default accounts for notification general


- Other taxes to be paid
- Penal interest to be paid
- Refunds etc. reducing payment
- Deduction of excess heath care insurance contribution payment

Default accounts for information on other self-assessed taxes


- 10 Lottery tax
- 16 Tax on insurance premiums
- 24 Amount withheld from purchases price for timber
- 68 Amount withheld from interest paid out
- 92 Amount withheld from dividend paid out
- 39 Source tax withheld from dividend (paid out to nonresidents)
- 69 Source tax withheld from interest (paid out to nonresidents)
- 84 Source tax withheld from interest income (of residents)

 

The account for withholding tax can be also changed in Management > Accounting info > Default postings > Default salary postings (new). New default posting can bee seen in both views, if the accounting is not done by row.

  • If the accounting is done by row the change in withholding tax in Default postings for taxes view effects only the Employers separate report. 

 

Changing default posting

1. Click Pen icon next to the account or select the category and click Change bookkeeping account.

 2. Select account from the window and click Continue.

  • If the chart of accounts must be modified click Edit chart of accounts.

3. The selected account will be changed for the selected category. The default account will only effect new receipts. 

 

 To be taken into account when changing defaults

Self-assessment taxes will take the accounting account from the most recent default posting rule.

  • If replacement report is done for self-assessment taxes which had used old default postings, the replacement receipts correction postings should be corrected to correspond the old reports postings.

articles.name: Earning holidays
articles.title: Earning holidays
articles.body:
When Procountor's holiday settings are on in the Employee register, the holidays can be earned when salaries are calculated. Automatic holiday earning will be discussed in this article.  

 

Situations when Procountor's automatic holiday calculation works

At the moment the holiday calculation is possible for:

  • 14 day or 35 hour holiday earning rule
  • holiday pay calculation standard divider 25
  • holiday pay calculation average hourly
  • holiday pay calculation average daily
  • holiday pay calculation with 9% or 11,5%
  • holiday pay calculation with work day divider
  • holiday pay calculation with right for time off
  • holiday bonus by 50% of holiday pay

Read more about the process of holiday calculation here. 

 

How does the automatic holiday calculation work?

When the holiday calculation settings are on in the Employee register, it is possible to earn holidays automatically when salaries are calculated. 

  • Holidays cannot be earned retroactively which means that the already earned holidays should be brought to Procountor by using Excel or by one employee at the time in Holidays view. 

1. Create a new salary slip in Payroll > New salary list. Choose the right holiday credit year and salary period. 

  • Salary periods are determined in Management > Salary info > Salary periods.

2. When holiday calculation is on, the Working time allocation section in the New salary slip view should be filled, in order to allocate the days and hours that the employee has worked. Procountor will calculate the earned holidays by using this information. 

  • Working days for holidays will be automatically filled in by using the workdays that are in the salary period.
  • Working hours for holidays should be filled in manually if there is an employee who has holiday calculation on and he is an hourly worker.
  • Working days for working hour reduction field affects cumulative working days, of which working hour reduction is calculated. The field is only active for employees whose earning method has been set to Days in Working hour reduction settings. Field value is prefilled, same way as calendar workdays. The figure can be adjusted for all employees in Date and settings, or individually in Employees.

 

  • Working hours and days should be filled in so that Procountor can calculate earned holidays based on the created salary slips. 
  • It is possible to add working days/hours to individual employee when employees have been added to the list (before Creating salary slips).
    • It is possible to fill in the working hours and days separately to all employees in the Salary slip view.

3. Select the employees to the salary list and create the list. After this select one salary slip from the list and move to the Salary slip view.  

  • In the Salary slip view the working hours and days are shown in the right corner. 
    • The Working time field is not tied to the Qty field in the salary row. Procountor calculates the holidays only from the Working time field. 
  • Procountor looks at the holiday settings of the employee when the salary slip is created and calculates the earned holidays according to the settings and already earned holidays. 
    • Working time field's heading Hours/Days/Actual workdays varies when the holiday earning settings is average hourly or monthly standard divider.

 

  • In a situation when the salary slips salary period goes over holiday credit year, the user must specify which part of the salary belongs to the previous credit year and which to the next year.
    • The salary rows should be divided into two rows and the earning periods can be used to specify which sum of the salary belongs to the specific holiday year.
    • If the rows are not divided the sum of the salary will go to that credit year in which the starting day of the salary period is. 
  • Slips which are Unfinished will calculate the earned holidays to Holidays view. 
  • Approved salary slips will freeze the holidays to the Holidays view according to the selected holiday pay settings. 
    • The working time allocation cannot be changed for the Approved salary slips. 
    • If the working time has to be corrected the salary slip must be turned to status Unfinished. Other option is to make the corrections straight to the Holidays view by hand.

 

 

4. Employees can see their remaining holiday days in the salary slip PDF if no other settings are made. 

  • Only those holidays are calculated to the remaining holidays, which can be used during the current holiday year. 
  • The holidays that are earned during the current holiday year are not calculated to the remaining holidays sum in the salary slip. 
  • It is possible to hide the remaining holiday days from the salary slip in the Usage settings by selecting (Management > Company info > Usage settings) Holiday info on salary slip: Hide remaining holidays on salary slip. 

 

 

More information about paying holiday pay in Procountor can be found here.

articles.name: Correcting employer’s separate report
articles.title: Correcting employer’s separate report
articles.body:
This page goes through correcting the employer’s separate report and possible error situations related to the report.

 

Unsent report

Changes in period’s salaries, like new or invalided salary slips or updated insurance contracts, are automatically updated to the already created and unsent report. When the report is opened next time, a window opens that notifies about the changes:

 

 

If the report has been saved but not sent, the report can be edited through the Edit report button or by opening the report directly from the list. Then the report’s manually added fields for example, contact person information or possible penalty or refund interests can be modified.

The report can also be deleted with the Delete button, after which a completely new report is created.

 

Incorrect information in a report that has been sent successfully

Errors noticed after sending the separate report can be fixed either by invalidating the report or with a replacement report. Income register instructs to use the replacement method.

 

Invalidation

In the following situations, invalidation of a separate report has to be used:

  • Correcting payer’s information
  • Correcting the pension policy number, if the contract information has been incorrect
  • Correcting the occupational accident insurance company’s identifier and insurance policy number
  • Exception to insurance information: not subject to Finnish social security, only if the sickness insurance’s payment’s amount changes

When invalidating the report, it should be considered that this method also invalidates the report in Incoming register.  In case you have made a replacement report for the separate report before the invalidation, please notice that the payment invoice of the period’s first report version stays in the program and it has to be handled.

 

Replacement report

Replacement report is created to the same period as the new separate report. When the replacement report is created, the program alerts that an employer’s separate report has already been sent for the period. A new report is created as a replacement report.

Procountor retrieves all the period’s salary slips to the report according to the payday and notifies Income register that a replacement report replaces the original report sent for the period. The report that was created before the replacement report goes to status Replaced. The report in the Replaced status can be invalidated if necessary. 

An accounting page and payment invoice are created of the new replacement report. Accounting entries of the previously created report are automatically reversed and new entries are created on the accounting page of the replacement report. The original separate report’s payment invoice is taken into consideration in the new invoice. The replacement payment invoice will include the difference of the first and replacement report.

Please notice when paying the invoice that there might be multiple invoices for the same period, if the replacement method has been used. 

In a situation where the employer’s separate report has been marked as reported elsewhere, possible corrections has to be done in Income register’s e-service. After clicking the Mark as reported elsewhere button, the separate report cannot be invalidated or deleted.

 

Error in sending the report to Income register

Errors in Incomes Register reports are displayed in the Incomes reports widget on the Procountor front page. 

In case there is an error in sending the report to Income register, first check the feedback of the error. When the feedback has been read and the cause of the error has been pinpointed, the cause of the error has to be fixed.

After the correction, the report with an error can be deleted by clicking the Delete button. After this, a new employer’s separate report has to be created for the same period and sent to Income register.

 

Possible error situations in creating employer’s separate report

At this moment, some of the Income register’s feedbacks are unnecessary. The notifications are caused by the slowness of the service. A new separate report without corrections can be send when, the information has been sent successfully with the earnings payment report but for the separate report there is an error message for example, about job title, Employee’s Pension Act contract or accident insurance contract. If the error recurs, Income register should be contacted to ensure that Income register has received the reports.

articles.name: Special situations related to salary types
articles.title: Special situations related to salary types
articles.body:
On this page we introduce special situations and incidents related to salary types. 

 

Automatic percentage calculation

Procountor provides automatic calculation to some of the salary types. It is generated by using the following formula:

Monthly worker Hourly worker
(monthly salary+fringe benefit)/working hours x payment% (Fringe benefit/base salary working hours+hourly salary)x payment%

If the hourly worker has 1 or 0 hours of hourly wage in the salary base the fringe benefits will not be taken into the calculation of overtime work.

Automatic percentage calculation is applied in these salary types, following the above-mentioned formula:

Night work allowance

  • 1230 Overtime, day 50%
  • 1231 Overtime, day 100%
  • 1232 Overtime, week 50%
  • 1233 Overtime, week 100%
  • 1234 Overtime, day 150%
  • 1235 Overtime, day 200%
  • 1236 Overtime, week 150%
  • 1237 Overtime, week 200%
  • 1238 x-overtime 50%
  • 1239 v-overtime 100%
  • 1410 Sunday work compensation
  • 1412 Sunday work allowance 30%
  • 1441 Evening work compensation 15%
  • 1442 Night work allowance 45%
  • 1443 Night work allowance 40%
  • 1444 Night work allowance 30%
  • 1445 Night work allowance 20%
  • 1453 Saturday work compensation 20%
  • 1454 Saturday work compensation 25%
  • 1455 Saturday work compensation 10%
  • 1456 Saturday work compensation 60%
  • 1492 work on a day before a holiday 50%
  • 1493 Holiday and religious holiday compensation 50%
  • 2521 Stand-by compensation 10 %
  • 2522 Stand-by compensation 25 %
  • 2523 Stand-by compensation 35 %
  • 2524 Stand-by compensation 70 %

 

Working hour reduction compensation

Salary types 1460 Working hour reduction compensation (3,6%) and 1461 Working hour reduction compensation (7,7%) take into account these salary types in the percentage calculation.

  • Salary for time worked – salary types (except 1461 and 1460 and 1462)
  • 2413 Sick leave allowance
  • 2510 Emergency work compensation
  • 2530 Training time wage
  • 2610 Meeting fee, all insurance
  • 2630 Lecture fee, all insurances
  • 2640 Shop steward fee, all insurance
  • 2900 Compensation for work

 

Holiday compensation for a short-term employment

2223 Holiday compensation for a short-term employment (excl. fringe benefits) and 2224 Holiday compensation for a short-term employment (incl. fringe benefits) takes into account the following salary types:

  • 1004 Hourly salary
  • 1005 Hourly salary, weekday evening
  • 1006 Hourly salary, weekday
  • 1007 Hourly salary, sunday evening
  • 1008 Hourly salary, sunday
  • 1012 Personal salary share (a share of hourly wages)
  • 1020 Pay per job
  • 1200 Extra work premium
  • 1220 Overtime compensation base
  • 1410 Sunday work compensation
  • 1411 Sunday work compensation (no automatic calculation)
  • 1412 Sunday work allowance 30%
  • 1441 Evening work compensation 15%
  • 1442 Night work allowance 45%
  • 1443 Night work allowance 40%
  • 1444 Night work allowance 30%
  • 1445 Night work allowance 20%
  • 1446 Evening work compensation, day before a holiday
  • 1447 Evening work compensation
  • 1448 Night work allowance
  • 1449 Sunday night work allowance
  • 1450 Sunday evening work allowance
  • 1451 Sunday night shift allowance
  • 1452 Evening work compensation
  • 1453 Saturday work compensation 20%
  • 1454 Saturday work compensation 25%
  • 1455 Saturday work compensation 10%
  • 1456 Saturday work compensation 60%
  • 1457 Saturday work compensation
  • 1462 Working hour reduction compensation (no automatic calculation) (only included in salary type 2224 Holiday compensation for a short-term employment (incl. fringe benefits))
  • 1492 Work on a day before a holiday 50%
  • 1493 Holiday and religious holiday compensation 50%
  • 2130 Bonus pay

 

Base salary deductions

Base salary deduction will be brought automatically to some specific salary types. 

  • The amount of the deduction row is negative.
  • Deduction row can be added manually from the salary type register. 

2411 Sick leave wage - month

  • Will be added to the salary slip with salary type 1017 Deductions from base salary, sick leave pay.

2208 Holiday pay, percentage

  • Will be added to the salary slip with salary type 1023 Base salary deduction, percentage, holiday pay
  • Base salary deduction row is calculated in a following way: (Monthly pay/ workdays from salary list) x workdays during holiday period

2203 Holiday pay, monthly wages

  •  Will be added to the salary slip with salary type 1014 Base salary deduction, leisure-time

2204 Holiday pay, monthly wages, standard divider 25

  • Will be added to the salary slip with salary type Base salary deduction, leisure-time, standard divider 25

2205 Leave for which holiday bonuses are paid, standard divider 25

  • Will be added to the salary slip with salary type 1016 Base salary deduction, leisure-time

 

Salary types without an income type code

Salary types that do not correspond to any income type can be found in the Procountor salary type register. When these salary types are used in the salary statement, the salary type does not send info to the income register.

Using the salary types you can manage payments on the salary slip that do not yet have to be notified to the income register. The payments may be related to, for example, a contract between the employer and employee, in which the employee withholds a certain payment, specified in the contract, from a person’s net earnings. 

The table below lists those salary types without a income type code. 

Income type 

Salary type 

Note

No code

Other taxfree compensations

Effect on only the net earnings. Not  part of the social insurance or pay-as-you-earn circle of influence.

No code

Trade union fee

Effect on only the net earnings. Not  part of the social insurance or pay-as-you-earn circle of influence.

No code

Party tax

Effect on only the net earnings. Not  part of the social insurance or pay-as-you-earn circle of influence.

No code

Health insurance fund fee

Effect on only the net earnings. Not  part of the social insurance or pay-as-you-earn circle of influence.

No code

Rent

Effect on only the net earnings. Not  part of the social insurance or pay-as-you-earn circle of influence.

No code

Loan repayment

Effect on only the net earnings. Not  part of the social insurance or pay-as-you-earn circle of influence.

No code

Interest 

Effect on only the net earnings. Not  part of the social insurance or pay-as-you-earn circle of influence.

No code

Private fund withdrawal from a company account

Effect on only the net earnings. Not  part of the social insurance or pay-as-you-earn circle of influence.

No code

Net liability

Effect on only the net earnings. Not  part of the social insurance or pay-as-you-earn circle of influence.

 

Effect on only the net earnings

Salary types not adjusted to the income register only affect the net salary paid to the employee. These salary types are not taken into account in pay-as-you-earn salaries and are not included in the social insurance circle of influence. The salary types are not taken into account in the handling of the Employees’ Pension Act, unemployment, accident, group life and health insurances. 

The Procountor salary type register contains several salary types, affecting only the net salary, because the use of the salary types in question varies depending on the situation. On the same salary slip you can manage, for example, the collection of rent and union membership payments from a person’s net salary. When these payments have their own salary types on offer you can also create accounting control for each salary type. 

Salary type Salary debt is meant as a help tool for  fixing salary info when it is necessary to correct the net shares an employee’s Employees’ Pension Act and unemployment insurance payments with a credit note. The salary type should not be used for any other purpose.

articles.name: Employees’ Pension Act (TyEL) contributions’ control data: Temporary employer
articles.title: Employees’ Pension Act (TyEL) contributions’ control data: Temporary employer
articles.body:
If an organization hires an employee for temporary work it should be reported to Income register with a report information about temporary employer. More information about when an employment is a temporary employment and the right method to report temporary employment can be found from company's pension insurance companies and income register. This instruction goes through how it is technically done in Procountor. 

 

Generic TyEL agreement number

When temporary employer's criteria is fulfilled the employer should give a generic TyEL agreement number in the Earnings payment report. This number should be fetched from the pension insurance companies. Here is a list of five different companies which provide the generic number. 

  • Elo 
  • Ilmarinen
  • Varma
  • Veritas
  • Pensions-Alandia

 

Saving the generic number to Procountor

The generic pension insurance number should be filled in to Procountor in order to be able to send Earnings payment reports to Income register. 

 

 

1. Go to Management > Salary info > Salary basic info > Employee's pension agreements.

2. Add a new pension agreement row.

3. Choose the company that has provided the number. Notice that each company has their own generic number and if the company and number does not match in the report the income register reporting will fail.

4. Add the generic pension agreement number. 

5. Put the agreement Active and some additional information can be filled to notice which agreement is which. 

6. Save the changes.

 

If the employer has to report that he is a temporary employer a tab should be put to Income register information: Temporary employer in Salary basic info view.

 

 

Selecting the generic agreement to the employee's salary info

 

 

1. Go to Payroll > Employee register > Select employee > Edit salary info.

2. In salary info view the pension type should be TyEL and the generic TyEL agreement is chosen from the drop down menu.

3. Calculate salaries for the employee.

articles.name: Employment info to present on earnings payment report
articles.title: Employment info to present on earnings payment report
articles.body:
The info regarding employee’s employment information and basic salary is defined on employee’s Salary info view. This article covers information about what is the info on employee’s Salary info view to be presented on earnings payment report to income register and what is the info needed just for executing salary calculations in Procountor.

The employment info is defined on employee’s Salary info view, which can be accessed by first opening the Employee register view (Payroll > Employee register). After executing a search in employee register, the employee-specific info can be accessed by clicking on the name of the employee. Salary info view can be accessed by clicking on the Salary info tab on the view.

 

Transferring the beginning and end date of the employment to the earnings payment report

Beginning date

When the beginning date of the employment is given to the Valid from field on the Salary info view, it will transfer to the earnings payment report.

Income register uses the word employment relationship in their instructions. The instructions tell that the beginning date of the employment relationship is the date, from which the employment relationship is continuous, i.e., the beginning date will not change if a temporary contract of employment is continued with another temporary contract or if there are several temporary contracts that are continuous together.

 

 

End date

When the end date of the employment is given to the Valid to field on the Salary info view, it will transfer to the earnings payment report. In Procountor, the reason of ending the employment must be given when giving the end date.

Income register’s instructions say that the end date of a temporary employment must be given the moment the payer knows the end date. The end date must also be given when a permanent employment relationship’s end date is on record or the employment relationship is already ended.

 

Reason for termination

In Procountor, it is mandatory to give a reason for ending the employment relationship when giving an end date of the employment relationship.

Reason for termination field offers the options for reasons according the reasons in the code of income register. 

 

 

 

Type

The info of relationship type in the Type field will not be transferred to the earnings payment report. Notifying the type and duration of the employment relationship to the income register is optional.

 

Registration grounds ID (Keva)

Registration grounds ID (Keva) field can be left empty in a situation, where the TyEL insurance does not concern Keva’s retirement pension insurance. The info in the field will transfer to the earnings payment report, so it cannot be used to any other purpose than where it is meant to.

 

Notifying the employment relationship information when the retirement pension institution is Keva

Beginning date

When the beginning date of the employment is given to the Valid from field on the Salary info view, it will transfer to the earnings payment report.

Income register uses the word employment relationship in their instructions. The instructions tell that the beginning date of the employment relationship is the date, from which the employment relationship is continuous, i.e., the beginning date will not change if a temporary contract of employment is continued with another temporary contract or if there are several temporary contracts that are continuous together.

 

Reason for termination

If the retirement pension company is Keva at the time the employment relationship ends, the end date and the reason for ending the employment relationship are mandatory information.

Retirement pension contract is defined on Salaries basic info view (Management > Salary info > Salaries basic info). If the retirement pension contract type is one of Keva’s retirement pension companies, the options to choose from in the Reason for ending the employment relationship field are updated according to Keva’s code.

 

 

Registration grounds ID (Keva)

If the employee’s retirement pension company is Keva, and the employee has several employment relationships, the Registration grounds ID (Keva) filed is mandatory to fill out on the Salary info view. The Keva’s code for registering and ending an employee relationship can be found here (in Finnish).

The concept of an employee relationship is wide in the Act governing retirement pensions of municipal employees, since along with employments and official ranks, also different assignments and confidential posts are considered as employment relationships. In Procountor, several, simultaneous, employment relationships can be saved to one employee.

On a Salary slip view, it is possible to define the employment relationship the slip is concerning. This way employment relationship specific salary slips can be created for the employee.

Based on the Act governing retirement pensions of municipal employees, only the employee’s earnings from employment relationships with the same registration grounds ID (Keva) can be notified with the same earnings payment report. If the employment relationships have different registration grounds ID (Keva), the earnings from the employment relationships must be notified with separate earnings payment report.

 

Employment relationship info to notify from Procountor

Employment relationship info must be given from Procountor to earnings payment report. In Procountor, the employment relationship info is managed in employee’s Salary info view (Payroll > Employee register, click on the name of the employee and the choose the Salary info tab.).

 

Mandatory info to notify

The beginning date of the employment relationship is always notified in the earnings payment report. In Procountor, the duty to notify is carried out by entering the beginning date of the employment relationship to the Valid from field in the Employments section on the Salary info view. if the employee has several employment relationships, they must be entered to the Employments section by clicking on New Employment button. The employment relationship the salary slip is concerning can be defined on the salary slip. The earnings payment report is formed based on the info on the salary slip.

The end date of the employment relationship and reason for termination must be notified on the earnings payment report, if the info is on the record. In Procountor, the info is entered to the Valid to and Reason for termination fields in the Employments section on the Salary info view. There are two codes for notifying the reason for termination; income register’s code and Keva’s code. The code to be used depends on the selected retirement pension institution.

The mandatory info mentioned above transfers to the earnings payment report.

 

Optional info to notify

Income register’s instructions also include detailed definitions of the optional information fields to notify.

Thus far the following optional information will not transfer to the earnings payment report: Whether or not the employee is in an employee relationship defined by income register, type of the employee relationship, duration of the employment relationship, part-time percentage, agreed working time per week and the type of the base salary.

 

Defining the employment relationship in Procountor

Info to be utilized in salary calculations can be saved to the Salary info view. Even the info will not transfer to the earnings payment report, it is needed in order to execute the salary calculations.

The Type of the employee relationship can be defined in the Employments section. There are several possible options to choose from, for example, permanent, temporary and part-time. The info in the Type field will not transfer to the earnings payment report but it provides essential information for the accountant calculating the salaries.

The type of the Base salary can be defined in the Income settings section. There are several possible options to choose from, for example, one month (total salary), compensation for work, payment by job and hourly. With the info on the field, it is possible to form a salary base, on which the employee’s salary slip is based on. Defining the base salary enables salary calculations.

 

Employment relationship info on the earnings payment report

The table below illustrates the info that can be notified to income register on the earnings payment report. In addition, the table illustrates the info that will not transfer from Procountor to earnings payment report.

articles.name: Salary payment
articles.title: Salary payment
articles.body:
Salaries can be paid when thy salary slips are have been Approved.

 

 

Salary payment methods

Salaries can be paid in two ways: as a salary payment or a regular bank transfer.

Salary payment is a payment method that has been developed specifically for paying salaries. When this payment method is used, the payment is debited from the payment account as a lump sum and the salaries will be transferred to employees’ bank accounts on the morning of the payday. This means that the payment follows the payment date (day when the payment is debited from the payment account) and the payday (day when the salary is on the employee’s account) that have been defined on the salary list regardless of the bank. 

The salary payment method can only be used when the payee’s bank account is in the SEPA area and the salary is paid in euros. The payee’s IBAN account number and BIC code are needed for the payment.

Payments can also be paid as regular bank transfers by paying all of the salary statements individually. In this case, please note that the salary might not be on the payee’s account exactly on the morning of the payday. Payment schedules depend on the payment time and the banks of the payer and employee. Another thing that needs to be noted when using bank transfers for salary payments is that payments will be shown on the bank statement as regular payments so that both the employee’s name and the payment sum are visible.

Payment schedules for the different payment methods can be found here. 

 

Implementing the salary payment method

Paying salaries in Procountor requires that the bank has installed payment services for the account that the company is using. In addition, the payment account information must be stored in Management > Company info > Bank account information.

The used payment methods are defined in bank account information. To be able to use Procountor’s salary payment function on the payment account, you must choose the payment method Salary payment in bank account information. If you are only using bank transfers, you can choose bank transfer in bank account information.

The selections made in bank account information do not automatically install payment services with your bank, as you have to make a separate agreement with the bank.

 

Salary payment function

 

 

An approved salary list can be paid as a salary payment in Salary list search by opening the salary list to be paid and selecting Salary payment under the Payment button. 

Salary statements on the salary list that have the status Approved can be paid in Salary payments. If a salary statement is not shown in the salary list’s Slip info column, it might have an incorrect status.

Payment information, including payment account, is chosen in New payment transaction. When payment information has been controlled, click the Pay salary list button.

After debiting, the salary list’s status will be Payment queued. This means the salary list is waiting for its due date (the payment date defined for the salary list) to transfer to the bank. If necessary, the salary list payment can still be cancelled in the same Salary payment view by clicking Cancel payment. The instructions for canceling the payment transaction can be found here. 

The status of the salary list will change to Payment sent to bank when Procountor has sent the salary data to the bank on the due date. The salary data can no longer be canceled at this point.

The payment transaction is shown as a bundle of whole salary payment. The individual employees cannot be seen in the bank statement. 

 

Payment transactions

Information on the payments made on the salary list, including payment date, total sum of payments and the account used for payments, is stored in Payment transactions in Salary payment.

If the payment of a salary list fails at the bank for some reason, customer service can remove the regular payment status of a salary list, after which payment transactions can be deleted from the list by clicking the Remove payment transaction button. The button removes the payment transaction from all salary slips in the list; you do not need to individually delete the transaction from each slip.

Unlike with the payment of other receipts, no information remains of previous, canceled, and deleted payment transactions in the Salary payment view. The view contains payment transactions only when the payment of the salary list has a status of Payment queued, Payment sent to bank, or Paid.

 

Bank transfer

 

 

If the salary payment function is not used for paying salaries, salaries can be paid as bank transfers from Procountor.

Begin the payment by opening a salary list and clicking Payment > Bank transfer. Select all payable salary statements from the view. When salary statements are selected, click Pay. Salaries will be transferred for payment in the first payment run of the due date selected for the salary. 

If necessary, select Use pay date to enter a payment date that deviates from the due date for all of the selected salaries. This way, the date entered in the payment date field will be used.

If a salary statement has a status that cannot be used for payments (for example Unfinished), the salary is shown in red and cannot be selected.

The individual employees to whom the salary has been payed can be seen in the bank statement.  

Paid elsewhere

Salaries can be set to the Paid elsewhere status if they are not paid from Procountor. This marking can be selected in the same view as paying bank transfers. Begin by opening the salary list, choose Payment > Bank transfer and choose salary statements from the list.

Before marking salaries as paid, control the payment date field for the salaries. If necessary, change the payment date to reflect the actual payment date. When the selections have been made, click Mark as paid elsewhere. Wages and salaries now have the status Marked paid.

articles.name: Setting up an employee: Salary base
articles.title: Setting up an employee: Salary base
articles.body:
Salary base can be found from Payroll > Employee register > Edit salary base.

 

 

Using the salary base

Once employees have been created in the employee register after having filled out the necessary information in the person register, you can fill out the Salary info and Salary base fields in the employee information section.

The Salary base can be found under: Payroll > Employee register > Select employee > Salary base.

The employee’s Salary base view functions as a model for the employee’s salary slips. When new salary slips are created for employees, the salary types and values from the salary base are imported automatically to the slips.

A default salary base is created based on the employee’s salary information, for example the amount of base salary is imported directly from salary information. The automatically created salary base can be completed with additional salary types, if necessary. It’s possible to save all salary types that are used often in salary calculation, so you do not need to import them separately during each salary calculation.

Salary slips -button searches all the salary slips that has been calculated to the employee. 

  • The same button can be found from all the salary base view pages (salary info, salary base, absences, holidays)

Write a note field is linked to salary slip write note field. 

  • If a note is written to salary base it can bee seen by the person who calculates the salary (not visible to employee). 
  • If something is written to the field in the salary slip the text is changed accordingly to the salary base. 
  • The field is meant to as a post it to the salary clerk. 

 

Salary base templates

Salary bases can be completed for employees manually, one by one, but creating a common salary base template is useful when the employees' salary bases are similar. Read more about salary base templates here.

Salary base basic rows

The base salary row information is transferred to the salary base from the employees salary info, including one Base salary row, the withholding tax row, Employees’ Pension Act row and unemployment insurance row.

  • If a person does not have to pay Employees’ Pension Act payments or accident insurance, these rows will be left out based on the ‘Salary info’ view commands. 
  • Base salary row cannot be deleted from the salary base. 
    • If the employee does not earn any salary that can be found from salary info view base salary drop down menu, the base salary row should be deleted from salary slip view every time salary is calculated. 

 

Adding a salary type to the Salary base

We recommend adding all salary types that are used frequently in a person’s salary slip to the salary base. When a salary type has been added to the salary base, it will be automatically imported to new salary slips. Salary type prices and other information can be edited in the salary slip, if necessary.

By clicking the Add salary type button, you can access the salary type search, from where you can import a salary type for a salary base. 

  • Nearly all Procountor's salary types are mapped to incomes register's income types. 
  • Own salary types cannot be created in Procountor. 
  • Select the suitable salary type from the salary type register and bring it to the salary base.

  • When a trade union (fixed / percentage-based) is added to an employee’s salary information, the 6042/6043 labor union salary type row is automatically added to the salary basis.  If the trade union is removed, the corresponding salary type is removed from the salary basis.

  • Distraint -Once Create distraint invoice automatically is enabled in the settings, distraint settings can be defined per employee. 

The car benefit and accommodation benefit can be fetched from the Benefit calculators button.

  • Read more about car benefit calculator here. 
  • read more about accommodation benefit calculator here. 

 

Salary type additional information

Certain salary types require additional information that is then forwarded to the salary info notification. When you have selected the row information for this kind of a salary type, the additional information fields will open. 

Employer’s insurance accruals

Employer’s insurance accruals can be viewed at the bottom of the salary base view. With this information, you can check that insurances in a person’s salary slip are handled correctly.

articles.name: Data security in Procountor
articles.title: Data security in Procountor
articles.body:
Data security is a crucial part of the Procountor's development and service provision. Data security includes the external and internal security of servers, verification of data in the service, the testing and monitoring of hardware and software, the confidentiality obligation of personnel, user identification and the encryption of data communications related to the software.

 

Server data security

  • The Procountor production environment operates on dedicated servers to which only authorized persons have access. The maintenance of our production servers is the responsibility of Advania.
  • The data center containing Procountor’s servers complies with the Finnish Communications Regulatory Authority’s 48B/2004M requirements for critical hardware rooms, and is thus appropriate for critical business systems requiring a high level of data security and usability. The data center service includes a high-quality power supply with backup power, cabling, ventilation, a fire protection system and physically secure facilities.
  • Procountor’s production and development environments are both equipped with fire and burglary alarm systems. The premises are also equipped with recording surveillance cameras. Only authorized persons have access to the data center and development environment, which have separate access control systems.
  • User rights to databases and information systems are secured through company, group and employee-specifically defined access rights. Only the use of tested and approved software is permitted in database processing, and the use of third-party management software is forbidden. Use of database traffic interfaces from external networks has been prevented.

 

Uninterrupted operation, safeguards and control

  • Particular attention has been paid to uninterrupted operation and fault tolerance in Procountor’s server environment. Fault-tolerant, reduplicated components are used in server hardware, and the disk systems in particular have been built to eliminate disruptions caused by physical disk errors. High usability of data communications services has been ensured through a reduplicated firewall and internet connections routed through the backbone networks of two operators.
  • Backup copies of all Procountor databases and files are made daily in a separate fire area, and changing data is constantly replicated onto a backup server, which minimizes the disruptions caused to service provision by hardware failure etc. The server room and service-provision space are monitored around the clock so that any problems can be identified and addressed as quickly as possible.

 

Testing and monitoring

  • The operation of firewall and other technology is tested on a regular basis. Attempts to gain unauthorized access to the data network and its services are monitored actively.
  • Procountor and its updates are tested in a separate testing environment before their actual launch. In addition to hardware and systems, the log files related to the program are monitored and analysed on a regular basis, as are error situations caused by users.
  • We actively obtain information through several channels on risks to the information system. On the basis of such information, we are able to prepare for any problems and eliminate them before they arise.

 

Professional competence and obligation to secrecy among personnel

  • Procountor personnel involved in service production receive training in the areas specified according to their duties.
  • All personnel working with confidential customer information have signed non-disclosure agreements.

 

User identification and rights

  • Users of Procountor software are authenticated using personal usernames, passwords, and single-use passwords for individual sessions. User rights can be flexibly defined by user and function. Data transfer between Procountor servers and users’ computers is encrypted using HTTPS technology.
  • Users must not disclose their personal usernames, passwords or single-use passwords to others. Procountor never asks users to disclose their passwords, single-use passwords or other confidential information by e-mail or other means. Issues related to the use of Procountor are communicated through main users and news items are displayed upon login.

 

About the program view

  • About the program view can be accessed through the Basics menu in the upper right corner of the page. On the view, you can check the current version of Procountor and the latest update time. Your operating system and browser information is also shown here.
  • In some situations, the customer service is interested in the browser in use by the customer. The information can be found in section Info about the customer’s browser on the About the program view. You can click the area and copy the text to your email.

articles.name: Dimension-specific limitation of user rights
articles.title: Dimension-specific limitation of user rights
articles.body:
Dimension-specific limitation of user rights is a chargeable additional service that is used to limit the user rights to specific dimensions and items. By using the dimension-specific limitation of user rights, it is possible to, for example, restrict user’s access only to his/her cost centers and projects on the level of income statement, balance sheet, general ledger and general journal.

More detailed information about the pricing and ordering of dimension-specific limitation of user rights can be found here. The function can be ordered also by contacting Procountor Customer service via contact form.

Note! Dimension-specific limitation of user rights can’t be activated in a Procountor environment that is using Document management additional service.

 

Setting up the limitations of user rights

After dimension-specific limitation of user rights has been activated in an environment, user-specific limitations can be set in Users and privileges view (in Management > Users and privileges). 

A new field of Limited dimensions is visible in the User right limitations section. In use is chosen in this field to activate the function. After this, the user-specific dimensions are can be determined by clicking Edit access button that is located in below.

Button opens User’s rights to dimension items view that is used to choose the desired items of specific dimensions:

 

 

No items are chosen by default. Items can be chosen one by one by marking the selection box on the left side of an item. If all items of one dimension are chosen, it is easier to use the topmost selection box that is located in line with the Item heading.

The chosen items are saved with the Save button.

HTML button is used to open the information in HTML format.

 

Effects of the limitations on creating and searching receipts

If a user is eligible to create e.g. sales invoices, he/she can create them normally. However, if an invoice is not dimensioned with the items that the user has access to, the user can’t search and find the invoice anymore after its creation.

A user can search and view those receipts that are dimensioned with the user-specific items. When invoices are searched in Receipt search, only invoices containing one or more user-specific items are shown in the search results. However, it should be noted that a user is able to see invoices that include also other dimensions or items if any user-specific item has been used on those invoices.

Other settings in the user rights determine if a user has only a right to view receipts or if he/she can also edit them.

 

Effects of the limitations on verifying and approving invoices

If a user is set as a verifier to an invoice that is dimensioned with other dimensions and items than the user-specific items, the user is mainly not able to verify this kind of invoice. This situation stands also with invoices that do not have dimensions at all.

However, an exception to the previous is possible when “Search for personal approvals only” restriction is activated in the user rights: this way the user is able to search for all invoices that are waiting for his/her verification or approval, even if the invoices do not have dimensions at all or have different dimensions and items than the user-specific items.

Nevertheless, after verifying or approving this kind of an invoice, the user can’t search or view the invoice later on.

 

Effects of the limitations on reporting

When dimension-specific limitation of user rights has been activated, graphical reports, such as Purchase and Sales reporting, Register-dimension reporting and Management reporting, are not available. Dimension-specific limitation of user rights deactivates also the following widgets from the front page: Cash and ledger tracking, Bank Account balance, Invoices waiting for verification, Result tracking, Revenue and profit development, Open sales invoices and Unpaid purchase invoices. Quick links in the front page are visible, but they can be used only with invoices that the user is allowed to view.

The user must have viewing rights for accounting reports in order to see user-specific transactions on the accounting reports. The user can view the reports only from the perspective of user-specific dimensions and items. The following accounting reports are available:

  • Income statement
  • Balance sheet
  • General journal
  • General ledger
  • Transactions by dimensions

 

Examples and notes on using the accounting reports

When dimension-specific limitation of user rights is activated, the search criteria of income statement and balance sheet automatically uses Allocated part search criterion that includes the user-specific dimension and items. If the user has rights to several dimensions, the Allocated part search criterion is added to the search criteria for each dimension by default.

The reports are only calculatory when Allocated part search criterion is used. This means that drilling down to single entries from the reports is not possible. More information about this particular search criterion and its application can be found here.

Instead of the Allocated part search criterion, it is also possible to add a search criterion named Dimensions from the New search criterion drop-down menu. With this search criterion, only the dimension or dimensions that the user is limited to can be selected. Allocated part search criterion can be deleted by clicking the X-button next to it.

When Dimensions search criterion is used and a dimension is chosen in the field, the user-specific items appear to the Items field. Only the user-specific items can be chosen for each user-specific dimension.

The reports show only those transactions that include the chosen dimensions and items when Dimensions search criterion is used. It is also possible to drill down to the level of single receipts from the report. This allows the user to see all receipts that include at least one user-specific item (even if the same receipts include also items that the user do not have rights to).

If no selections are made in Dimensions menu and Items menu and/or Dimensions search criterion is not included in the search criteria, and Allocated part search criterion is also not used, the reports will include total values of receipts that include at least one user-specific item.

 

Effects of other limitations on reporting

If “Personal … only” limitations (e.g. “Personal purchase invoices only”) have been set to a user in addition to the user-specific limitations of dimensions and items, the user can search only receipts that meet both of these conditions.

For example, if a user has user-specific items and “Personal purchase invoices only” limitation, the user can search only those purchase invoices that include the user-specific items and that the user has created himself/herself. If only one of these conditions is met, the user can’t see this kind of invoices.

When “Personal … only” limitations are used in addition to the user-specific limitations of dimensions and items, accounting reports are still created only by the limitations of user-specific dimensions and items. This means that the reports will include also receipts that are created by someone else than the user in question. However, the user is not able to drill down to individual purchase invoices from the accounting reports. Instead, he/she can only see the total sum of receipts and the number of them.

 

How to terminate the service?

  • Our period of notice is one month, the agreement ends at the end of the agreement period month.
  • Please send all notices of termination through the form feature in Management > Company info > Basic info > Contract and product changes. From the Change requests drop-down menu, select Other request. The required information in the message includes the name of the company name, business ID and which service you want to terminate. Alternatively, you can contact us by email to hallinto@procountor.com.

articles.name: Archived financial statements
articles.title: Archived financial statements
articles.body:
The closed fiscal year’s financial statements can be viewed conveniently in the Archived financial statements view, which aggregates the financial statements. The view can be accessed through Accounting > Archived financial statements.

 

 

When the financial year is closed, the following reports are automatically saved to the archived financial statements:

  • Chart of accounts
  • Income statement
  • Balance sheet
  • General journal
  • General ledger

These reports are formed into the archive according to the program’s default search criteria so that all the entries that are interpreted as transactions are exported to the report from the start to the end of the fiscal year. The income statement and balance sheet are formed so that every account that has a balance is presented as their own row.

The reports will show up to the archived financial statements after the update during the night. This means that they can be viewed the day after the fiscal year has been closed. If the closed fiscal year is opened again for example for corrections, the already created reports remain in the archive. When the fiscal year is closed again later, the reports of the fiscal year that are in the archive will be replaced with the new updated reports.

In addition to the reports mentioned above, the following documents can also be exported to the archived financial statements:

  • Balance sheet itemisation: The balance sheet itemisation can be exported to the archived financial statements through the Balance sheet itemisation view’s Export to archive button.
